Bedford

About Cambridge Maintenance Services Limited

Cambridge Maintenance Services is a nationwide supplier of mechanical and electrical building services maintenance with over 34 years of experience in delivering its building services maintenance to the corporate, healthcare, education, retail, transport and manufacturing sectors. It also ensures optimum energy efficiency for every property portfolio it manages.

We are experts in delivering compliant, safe, and efficient workplaces. Our nationwide building services maintenance solutions span the corporate, healthcare, education, retail, transport, and manufacturing sectors. Using advanced technology and data, we provide cutting-edge maintenance services that are trusted by major managing agents and independent clients alike. As a multi-award-winning business, our local teams are dedicated to providing personalised FM services that meet your specific needs.

Job Description:

As a key member of our Electrical maintenance team, you'll play a vital role in delivering both planned and reactive maintenance across a range of electrical systems within our client portfolio. You'll be responsible for ensuring equipment operates safely and efficiently while providing an exceptional service that consistently exceeds customer expectations.

Everything you need to do the job will be provided, including a company van, mobile phone, tablet and uniform.

Key Responsibilities:

• Deliver exceptional service to our clients, ensuring all work is completed to the highest standards and in line with contractual requirements.
• Carry out planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and respond promptly to reactive maintenance and equipment breakdowns.
• Diagnose and rectify faults efficiently, arranging equipment replacements where required to minimise downtime.
• Complete quality inspections and ensure all work meets recognised industry standards and best practices.
• Effectively manage and maintain records through our Elogbooks facilities management system.
• Work closely with the Lead Engineer and Support Desk Supervisor to coordinate maintenance schedules, priorities, and reporting requirements.
• Participate in the out-of-hours emergency call-out rota as required.
• Undertake a variety of hands-on and physically demanding tasks across client sites.
• Ensure full compliance with company policies, health & safety legislation, and relevant industry regulations.
• Take ownership of your professional development by participating in training and maintaining up-to-date technical knowledge and qualifications.
• Build positive working relationships with clients and colleagues, representing the business professionally at all times.
• Support the wider team by undertaking additional duties appropriate to the role when required.

Hours of Work:

42.5 hours per week between Monday - Friday. Overtime starting after 47.5 hours.

Essential Skills & Qualifications:

• Good understanding of Electrical building services.
• Relevant Electrical Installation qualification (e.g. NVQ Level 3 or equivalent).
• 18th Edition.
• Full UK driving licence.
• Strong electrical fault-finding and diagnostic skills.
• Ability to interpret and analyse electrical systems.
• Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
• Methodical approach to record keeping and reporting.
• Practical, hands-on attitude with excellent problem-solving skills.

Desired Skills & Qualifications:

• Emergency Lighting Regulations.

• LV Approved.

title: Senior Account Executive
description:
Our Purpose

Scheduling isn’t simply filling shifts. It’s finding the sweet spot that enables businesses to grow and team members to enjoy the perfect work/life balance.

At Planday from Xero, we aim to use Agentic AI to build a future where managers seamlessly can free up invaluable time for their business and teams. We’re not just building software; we’re on a mission to make shift work more human, to change work/life balance from a luxury to a reality for all shift workers. We’re using advanced technology to help humans reach their full potential. At work and in life.

Founded in 2004, Planday is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark and helps create perfect schedules for hundreds of thousands of users across the world. Planday was acquired by Xero in 2021.

How You’ll Make An Impact

As a Senior Account Executive, you will drive new business growth by owning and developing your territory. You will lead complex sales cycles end to end by deeply understanding mid market and Enterprise customer challenges and translating Planday’s capabilities into clear operational value for their business.

You will operate with a high degree of autonomy, taking ownership of pipeline creation, deal progression, and forecast accuracy, and bringing a strong point of view on how Planday creates value for customers.

What You’ll Do

• Own and grow your territory with accountability for new ARR
• Build and progress pipeline through proactive prospecting and account planning
• Take end-to-end ownership of the sales funnel, from outbound cold prospecting, multi-channel outreach, and self-sourcing pipeline to running demos and closing.
• Map key accounts across UK shift-intensive sectors (hospitality, care, retail, events) and build targeted outbound campaigns.
• Lead full sales cycles with multiple stakeholders and longer decision processes
• Run high-quality discovery to understand customer challenges and position value clearly
• Lead customer discovery, deliver tailored product demos and lead commercial negotiation to provide solutions aligned to customer needs
• Maintain strong pipeline hygiene and forecasting discipline
• Collaborative, low-ego approach and ability to work across teams to win priority opportunities and improve execution

What You’ll Bring With You

• 2+ years of experience as a full-cycle / 360 B2B SaaS Account Executive, with a strong track record of self-sourcing pipeline.
• Track record of consistently closing new business through self-directed sales activity
• Experience selling to mid-market and enterprise customers with complex needs
• Strong commercial judgment and ability to manage your own territory as a business
• Excellent discovery, communication, and negotiation skills
• Comfortable running technical product demos and adapting them to customer use cases
• Comfortable operating with autonomy, structure, and accountability
• Curious, resilient, and motivated by building something rather than inheriting it
• Experience selling into workforce-intensive industries such as healthcare, hospitality or retail is preferred.

Success looks like

• Consistent delivery against new business targets
• Healthy, self-generated pipeline with strong conversion
• Accurate forecasting and disciplined deal management
• Clear ownership of outcomes and continuous improvement in execution

This position description is intended merely as a guideline of the responsibilities involved in the position. The employee is expected to perform any other duties as reasonably required by their Manager.

At Planday, we offer you

• Benefits like pension, health insurance, inclusive support for new parents and generous vacation
• On top of your annual base salary, you are offered to be part of an Employee Share Plan
• Growth and progression opportunities – we want you to grow with us
• Flexible remote work
• Strong social culture with lots of team and company activities
• Meaningful work – everyone at Planday contributes to improving the lives of shift workers around the globe
• Healthy work-life balance and autonomous approach to work. We trust in you and your abilities

Finally, our offices are not just workplaces (although they are pretty nice and well-located, we have to say!). Plandayers are open and welcoming and at Planday, everyone has the freedom and support to show their true self at work.

At Planday, we firmly believe that diversity and inclusion are the cornerstones of innovation and a vibrant workplace culture, and we highly value the strength that diverse backgrounds offer.

As an equal opportunity employer, we strive to create an equitable experience for all our candidates throughout the process. Please let us know if you need reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process.

All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to any personal characteristics.

title: Warehouse Section Leader - Nights
description:
At Gist, we're proud to be part of the M&S Group, the logistics engine behind M&S Food.

From our distribution centres to our transport operations and support functions, we connect people, technology and expertise to ensure the right products reach the right stores at the right time.

As we continue to invest in our people, technology and network, there's never been a more exciting time to join Gist and help shape the future of food logistics.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Night Warehouse Section Leader to join our Hemel Hempstead (Maylands) team.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you'll take ownership of a warehouse operation, leading your team to deliver outstanding service while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality and productivity.

Working closely with the Shift Manager, you'll be responsible for creating a positive team culture, coaching colleagues to succeed and ensuring your area operates efficiently throughout every shift.

Role Details

Salary: Up to £35,000 per annum + £4,500 Night Shift Premoim

Hours: 40 hours per week

Working Pattern: Nights – 4 on 4 off

Working Hours: 18:00 PM - 06:00 AM

Location: Hemel Hempstead (Maylands), HP2 7PZ

What You'll Be Doing

Your key accountabilities will include:

• Leading a team within your designated warehouse area, ensuring daily operational plans are delivered safely and efficiently.
• Providing clear direction, coaching and regular feedback to colleagues to support performance and development.
• Creating a positive, inclusive working environment where colleagues feel supported, motivated and able to perform at their best.
• Monitoring operational performance and delivering key service, productivity and quality KPIs.
• Supporting the induction of new colleagues and ensuring mandatory operational and legal training is completed.
• Conducting Return to Work interviews and supporting colleague wellbeing through proactive people management.
• Promoting a strong safety culture by identifying risks, resolving issues and ensuring compliance with health and safety procedures.
• Responding quickly to operational challenges, making decisions that keep the operation running smoothly.
• Encouraging continuous improvement by listening to colleague feedback and implementing practical ideas that improve performance.
• Working collaboratively with other operational teams to ensure excellent customer service and operational excellence.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys leading people in a fast-paced warehouse environment and takes pride in delivering high operational standards.

Your Skills And Experience Will Include

• Previous experience in a warehouse supervisory, team leader or section leader role.
• Experience leading and motivating operational teams within a busy warehouse or logistics environment.
• The ability to coach colleagues, provide constructive feedback and build high-performing teams.
• Strong communication and organisation skills with the confidence to make decisions under pressure.
• A proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement.
• Good understanding of warehouse operations and operational KPIs.
• Experience using Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) or similar operational systems.
• A commitment to maintaining high standards of safety, compliance and customer service.

What's in it for you?

As Well As a Competitive Salary, You'll Benefit From

• £35,500 annual salary
• Up to £4,500 Night Shift Premium
• 20% M&S discount on most things from furniture, fashion and food
• Discounted healthcare cash plan
• Auto Enrolment Pension or competitive Defined Contribution Pension Scheme and life assurance (up to four times salary)
• Amazing perks and discounts via our App to major retailers and restaurants
• Access to our Employee Assistance Programme and a wide range of wellbeing support
• A tailored induction and ongoing learning and development opportunities
• Cycle to Work scheme

description:

title: Laboratory Technician
description:
Location: Plymouth, UK (On-site – Candidates must be located in or close to Plymouth)

Position Type: Full-time

About Pulsiv

Pulsiv is disrupting the global power electronics industry. Our patented power conversion technology fundamentally changes how energy is converted—eliminating waste, boosting efficiency, and shrinking system footprints.

We are preparing for a massive phase of growth. With our flagship USB-C fast-charging platform launching in 2027, we will rapidly scale that technology across multiple power levels and variants. From there, we are expanding into high-power, high-growth markets including TVs/displays, LED lighting drivers, industrial power supplies, and hyper-scale data centers, among others. If you want to work on hardware that directly impacts global energy consumption across next-generation tech, this is where it happens.

The Role & Your Future at Pulsiv

We are looking for an ambitious, hands-on Laboratory Technician based in or within easy commuting distance of our engineering hub in Plymouth. This isn’t a passive bench job—you will be right at the heart of our R&D engine, building, tweaking, and stress-testing the prototype hardware that powers our technology roadmaps.

Because we operate as a lean, agile engineering team, this role requires a true "all-hands-on-deck" attitude. You will take full ownership of the laboratory space, handling everything from high-precision electronic assembly down to general lab upkeep, waste management, and day-to-day facilities tasks.

Where can this take you?

Pulsiv is scaling quickly, and we believe in growing our talent from within. As you master our lab systems and gain deep exposure to cutting-edge AC-to-DC conversion, this role offers a clear pathway to transition into Applications Engineering, Test & Validation, or Design Engineering. You won't just keep the lab running; you will build the technical foundation to launch a high-impact career in power electronics.

What You’ll Be Doing:

• Build & Modify Next-Gen Hardware: Hands-on prototyping, fine-pitch SMD/TH soldering, complex PCB rework, and custom cable assembly for cutting-edge power electronics modules.
• Drive Bench Testing & Validation: Set up thermal, efficiency, and environmental stress tests under engineering guidance, logging critical data for upcoming USB-C platforms, display power supplies, lighting drivers, and data center reference designs.
• Rapid Prototyping & 3D Printing: Own the lab’s 3D printers to fabricate custom test jigs, thermal fixtures, and mechanical prototype enclosures.
• Lab Ownership & General Housekeeping: Maintain a clean, safe, and professional laboratory environment. This includes routine facility support tasks such as emptying bins, managing recycling/waste clearance, organizing benches, and keeping walkways clear and hazard-free.
• Stock & Inventory Management: Oversee component stock levels, unpack shipments, track lab consumables, organize hand tools, and coordinate component re-ordering.
• Support Engineering Sprint Execution: Assist senior engineers with teardowns, equipment calibration tracking, schematics checks, and test automation setup.

What We’re Looking For:

Essential:

• Location: Based in or located close to Plymouth, UK (this is a fully on-site laboratory role).
• Degree Qualified: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
• Bench & Soldering Craft: Solid hands-on assembly experience, fine-pitch SMD rework, wire harness fabrication, and mechanical assembly skills.
• Test Tool Mastery: Familiarity with standard electronics lab equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, power analyzers, DC electronic loads).
• Schematic Literacy: Ability to confidently read electronic schematics, assembly diagrams, and technical datasheets.
• Software Competency: Comfortable using Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Teams) for logging data, tracking stock, and daily collaboration.
• Attitude: Flexible, proactive, and willing to get stuck into any task—big or small—to keep the engineering environment running smoothly.

Desirable (Bonus Points):

• Experience or familiarity with Altium Designer (schematic capture, PCB layout viewing, component placement).
• Hands-on exposure to thermal imaging cameras and 3D CAD/slicing software (Cura, PrusaSlicer, SolidWorks).
• Familiarity with high-voltage laboratory safety practices and ESD control environments.

Assistant Store Managers also are responsible for accomplishing administrative and operations focused activities, including floor management and scheduling.

Operations

Budget Responsibility

• Accountable for delegated aspects of controllable budget or labour hours

People Management

• Team lead role indirectly responsible for subset of store employees during shift or as delegated by Store Manager

Key Skills & Core Values You Bring

• Integrity/Honesty: Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner
• Leadership: Is able and desires to lead, influence, and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work
• Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve goals; seeks partnerships and diverse perspectives
• Adaptability/Agility: Tolerates uncertainty and ambiguity and can change priorities in a fast-paced environment
• Decision Making: Uses logic and reasoning to evaluate alternatives and make effective, timely decisions
• Strategic Thinking: Sets strategies that are aligned to vision and values of the company to achieve goals/vision/further the mission; considers the 'big picture' implications of decisions
• Resilience: Remains persistent; recovers quickly from setbacks

Job Requirements

Eligibility

• Must be 18 years of age or older
• Must have proof of the Right to Work and evidence relating to associated local legislative requirements (EMEA only)
• Must have the ability to travel to assigned store

Availability

• Willing to work a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays

Other Willingness Requirements

• Willing to work as part of a team and also complete work independently
• Willing to move through a store for most of a shift to help guests and accomplish work
• Willing to move boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg)
• Willing to work in an environment with bright lights and loud music

Experience

• Work experience in leadership or people management

Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)

• Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent
• Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
• Experience: 1 year retail or sales specific management experience

In keeping with our mission, please connect with us at accommodations@lululemon.com if you have questions about how your unique abilities may translate to the requirements for this role, with or without a reasonable accommodation. In your email, please include the position title, the location of the position and the nature of your question or request.

Beyond The Paycheck (Benefits & Perks)

At lululemon, we care for and invest in the whole person – body, mind, spirit. Our total rewards program is designed to support you in achieving your goals and focus on the things you love. description:
Cardiff

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and up to 30 days of annual leave.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

We have a brand-new opportunity for a Principal or Associate Electrical Engineer to join our team based in our Cardiff office and work as part of the largest independent consulting engineering firm of its kind. Joining at an exciting period in the Hoare Lea Cardiff journey, in our new City Centre Office.

Cardiff itself is a thriving and dynamic creative capital city with a rich cultural heritage, as well as ambitious future plans in terms of growth as well as a blueprint to become a carbon-neutral city in the next 10 years.

You will join a talented, dynamic, and diverse team of designers, engineers, and technical specialists with a unique working culture. Our team is large enough to work on large national and international schemes yet agile enough to allow significant talent growth and career progression.

As a Principal or Associate Engineer, you will be responsible for supporting and delivering designs for a range of project types and sizes. You will work within a multidisciplinary team of engineers and consultants delivering design solutions of the highest standard for our clients, while securing repeat and new business opportunities. A critical aspect of this role is to support and develop a team of technically competent, collaborative, and highly engaged team members.

In this key and varied role, you can expect to:

• Be responsible for the day-to-day technical delivery of the electrical design services for multi-disciplinary projects across a number of building sectors.
• Lead the development of initial strategic concepts for projects ensuring solutions are appropriate for the brief and regulatory standards.
• Interact regularly with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring a communicative, collaborative and timely approach to delivery This is a client-facing role, so you will be attending project meetings and disseminating / translating the brief within the project team.
• Work with the team leader to help monitor fee expenditure, resources and work delivered.
• Mentor and support our ‘next gen’ professionals, including apprentices and graduates.

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

• Proven experience working as an Electrical Engineer or in a closely related role, with a track record delivering on a variety of complex projects.
• Experience of modern technical delivery processes, and use of relevant software/tools such as BIM, Revit, Electrical OM, Dialux and Relux.
• Demonstrable experience working with clients/contractors / architects in a design-oriented / consultant role.
• Self-awareness, an open mind, and a spirit of generosity
• Experience in supporting others to develop knowledge, skills, and confidence.

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application, or for further information please contact aureliacherradi@hoarelea.com

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange a introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices.

We have updated our terms and conditions for candidates, click here to find out more.

title: 2027 Building Services Design Engineer - Degree Apprentice - Oxford
description:
2027 Building Services Design Engineer – Degree Apprentice

Oxford

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

Why Join Us?

• You’ll collaborate with the industry’s best, working with a wide range of built-environment specialists.
• You’ll be part of progressive and exciting projects from day one, able to experience innovative schemes across all sectors.
• You’ll advance your career, your way, thanks to our structured Career Paths framework.
• You’ll be encouraged through our accredited training and development scheme with a dedicated mentor and supervisor, supporting you to Chartership, if you wish.

Joining us is the chance to play your part in the future of engineering design. Our projects span scales, styles, and geographies. We’re committed to sustainable design, innovation, and collaboration with forward-thinking clients. Straight away you’ll experience working on live projects.

The Role

Being part of one of the UK’s largest building engineering consultancies, we benefit from collaborating with some of the best engineers in the business, with access to state-of-the-art technical support, and have the opportunity to work on some of the largest and most high-profile projects as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

Bispebjerg Hospital in Denmark, Canolfan Pentre Awel in Carmarthen, Multi-Megawatt Data Centre Campus , Oxford North in Oxford, One Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester, Gwynfaen in Swansea, and the nature-based net-zero neighbourhood of Earls Court in London, are examples of some of the amazing projects where we have led the design with other Hoare Lea disciplines.

As an Apprentice, your day-to-day tasks will vary, as we’ll expose you to all aspects of our work so you can discover what suits you. You could be;

• Working on live projects from day one – our exciting projects
• In a variety of sectors from healthcare to hotels, retail to residential
• Producing detailed designs and drawings
• Using the latest computer modelling software
• Undertaking site surveys
• Researching ground-breaking technologies
• Having regular meetings with project teams, clients or end users
• Preparing engineering system designs on computers
• Writing specifications
• Monitoring progress on construction sites.

There could be opportunities to specialise in electrical, mechanical or digital engineering design.

Communicating will span all of these, as we regularly liaise with project teams, meet clients or end users, and attend collaborative meetings.

Training

Apprenticeship - Building services engineer / Skills England

Provider – Building Services Design Engineering Apprenticeship BEng (Hons) | London South Bank University

You will develop and enhance your technical and management skills in a variety of applications and job roles, including design and project management. Additional learning support is provided in-house, and you will receive mentoring and supervision throughout your Apprenticeship.

You will receive one day study leave during term times to attend university to work towards your BSc or BEng Building Services Engineering degree providing a route to gain Incorporated Engineer (IEng) status.

The typical duration for this apprenticeship is 60 months, but this will depend on the previous experience of the apprentice and opportunities to gain the full range of competence.

About You

To be successful in this role, you’ll need…

• To meet the University’s entry requirements either;

• Three A levels at BBC including Mathematics and preferably a Science in either Chemistry or Physics; or
• T-Level at Merit or above in Construction: Design, Surveying and Planning, or similar; or
• BTEC Level 3 Extended Diploma DDM in an Engineering subject or above, with a minimum of Merit in Mathematics and Further Mathematics; or
• BTEC Level 3 National Diploma D*D* in an Engineering subject or above, with a minimum of Merit in Mathematics and Further Mathematics; or
• Level 3 or Level 4 Building Services Design Technician Apprenticeship; or
• A career on the tools e.g. an Electrician or a Mechanic, who wants to move into an office setting.

• Genuine interest in developing a career within the sector
• Excellent communication, analytical and organisational skills
• Ability to work in a team environment and independently
• A friendly, ambitious and confident individual with a flexible and resilient approach

Our Benefits

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer both core and flexible benefits, a competitive salary and industry leading training and development to support you throughout your career. We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality.

You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile, answer a couple questions, and submit your application. For hints and tips in applying click here .

Please only apply for one location for your discipline, if you are flexible with location, great! – you will have the chance to select your other location preferences, and this will be confirmed again with you at telephone interview. If you apply for multiple locations, you will only be considered for the location you have applied for.

Please note: We do not offer visa sponsorship for this apprenticeship role. Only candidates already authorised to work in the UK – e.g. British/Irish citizens, EU Settled/Pre-Settled, ILR holders – will be considered.

Recruitment Process

Our Projects Are Human-centric, And So Is Our Recruitment Process. Once You’ve Applied, You’ll Speak To a Person Every Step Of The Way. Here’s Our Planned Timeline

• Applications close – 6 th November 2026
• Telephone Interviews – November/December 2026
• Selection Event – January/February 2027

title: Mobile Vehicle Technician - Portsmouth
description:
Join the RAC as a Mobile Vehicle Technician in our SMR Division - a new era of mobile repair.

• A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000
• A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities
• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Portsmouth cluster, covering areas like Portsmouth, Havant, Waterlooville, Fareham, Gosport, Chichester, Emsworth. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability
• Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000. It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward.
• Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings.
• Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays. We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments.
• Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term.
• Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16+, offering reassurance whenever you need it.
• Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success.

Who thrives here?You’re more than just great with tools - you’re great with people. Our Mobile Mechanics are the face of the RAC: working on driveways, in car parks, speaking directly with members, and providing reassurance, clarity and high-quality service.

You enjoy independence, problem solving and real variety - each job is different. From servicing and diagnostics to in depth repairs and reporting, you’re hands-on, adaptable and confident making decisions on the spot.

You take pride in using your technical ability to genuinely help people and keep them moving.

The role is ideal if you want:✔ Independence in a mobile role

✔ The stability and support of a trusted national organisation

✔ Ongoing development, including future EV and diagnostic skills

✔ A role where giving members complete peace of mind is simply part of what you do

We’re the RACAt the RAC, we don’t stand still. With over 125 years of history and 12.5 million members, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

Our culture reflects that ambition - backed by a 4.5-star Glassdoor rating, our people know we’re serious about career growth, recognition, and support.

We celebrate individuality and champion every voice. As an equal opportunities' employer, we welcome people from all backgrounds and walks of life - it’s what sets us apart and drives us forward.

title: Fire Sprinkler Site Supervisor
description:
Department: M&E - Delivery

Location: Edinburgh

Description

Harmony is on a mission to be the best life safety partner to work with and for. Rated an ‘Outstanding Employer’ by Best Companies in 2025, we are only getting bigger and stronger — and we’re looking for A-players to help us get there.

We are passionate about making a difference and obsessed with quality. Our goal is to build a world where every resident can sleep safely at night, knowing their home is 100% safe.

We have an opportunity for a Fire Sprinkler Site Supervisor to join our M&E Projects team in Edinburgh. You will oversee the installation of fire sprinkler systems across a range of residential and commercial sites — leading your team on the ground, holding standards high, and ensuring every project is delivered safely, compliantly, and to the quality our clients expect.

This is a field-based role requiring flexibility across multiple sites. If you have strong sprinkler installation experience, natural leadership, and the drive to do things properly every time — this is the role for you.

Key Responsibilities

• Supervise and lead the on-site installation of fire sprinkler systems across residential and commercial projects, ensuring works are delivered safely, on programme, and to specification.
• Quality and Compliance — Ensure all sprinkler installation works are completed to Harmony, LPS 1048, BS EN 12845, and industry standards. Carry out timely checking of works on site and ensure accurate data input and record keeping throughout.
• Site Management — Oversee site set up and sign off, stock management, delivery of prelims, pre-condition surveys, and post inspections to allow for final sign off by the Project Manager. Identify and flag variation opportunities immediately.
• People Management — Resolve day-to-day issues, boost team morale, manage conflict, and identify resource requirements. Maximise the productivity and utilisation of colleagues and subcontractors on site.
• Quality Control — Ensure all works are certifiable and compliant, delivered to both client and Harmony expectations. Carry out regular spot checks and record findings accurately.
• Client Management — Attend pre-start meetings and ensure the site is always tidy and representative of Harmony’s brand. Carry out onsite resident liaison where required and communicate works clearly to those affected.
• Communication — Provide regular progress updates to the Project Manager and weekly reports to the client. Attend calls as needed and agree reporting frequency with the Project Manager.
• Health and Safety — Implement Harmony’s H&S policy across all sites. Induct new trades, ensure completion of all relevant H&S paperwork, deliver regular toolbox talks, and maintain a safe working environment through ongoing training and auditing.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

• An A-player mindset — high standards, extreme ownership and the drive to do things properly, the first time.
• Proven experience in a mechanical supervisory or senior trades role, with a background in fire sprinkler systems and associated mechanical systems.
• Experience running projects to time and on budget across multiple sites.
• Comfortable working flexibly across Glasgow and Edinburgh, with a willingness to travel as required.
• A strong problem solver who sees things through to completion.
• Ability to build and maintain good working relationships with clients, subcontractors, and colleagues.
• Proactive, confident, tenacious, and resilient.

Job Benefits

This is a chance to take on a field supervision role at one of the UK’s fastest-growing fire safety specialists — leading mechanical works across Scotland, with the tools, support and autonomy to do the job properly. At Harmony, we ask a lot — and we give a lot back. The hours are real, the standards are high and the work is demanding, but for those who show up, deliver and go the extra mile, the rewards follow. A-players here enjoy a competitive salary, a company vehicle, a Personal Development Plan with ongoing training and mentoring, unlimited holiday, a bonus scheme paying up to 50% of annual salary, enhanced maternity and paternity, lunch, snacks and refreshments on us every day at the office (fresh fruit and Takeaway Friday included), a team social budget, cycle to work, an auto-enrolment pension, two major company events a year and our Reward and Recognition scheme — including European mini-breaks for those who go above and beyond. It is a collaborative, high-energy environment focused on doing things the right way — and none of it is a perk for showing up; it’s what we share with the people pulling the business forward.

Harmony is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all applicants for employment regardless of age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief. We want everyone who works with us to feel valued and to make a difference.

group: uk centre for ecology & hydrology (ukceh)|business development lead
title: Business Development Lead
description:
How can organisations navigate the rapidly evolving landscape of nature finance, biodiversity disclosure and environmental markets with confidence?

From emerging nature-related disclosure frameworks such as the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) to the growth of Biodiversity Net Gain and early biodiversity credit markets, organisations are increasingly seeking trusted scientific expertise to inform business and investment decisions. UKCEH is uniquely positioned to meet this demand, bringing together some of the UK's leading expertise in ecosystem assessment, species monitoring, land use change and nature-based solutions, underpinned by world-class environmental science and data.

As our Nature Finance Business Development Lead, you will play a pivotal role in unlocking the commercial potential of UKCEH's science, helping organisations navigate emerging nature and biodiversity frameworks while creating opportunities for scientific impact at scale. Acting as UKCEH's lead commercial representative within the nature finance sector, you will build strategic relationships with corporates, financial institutions, government organisations and nature market developers, identifying where our scientific expertise can deliver meaningful value.

Working closely with scientists, research leaders and commercial colleagues, the post-holder will lead business development activities, develop strategic partnerships and grow a strong pipeline of commercial opportunities across the evolving nature finance market. Nature finance is the primary focus, but you will also pursue adjacent opportunities in environmental data, land use and natural capital where UKCEH's science is a strong fit. Combining commercial acumen with excellent relationship-building and communication skills, you will translate market needs into impactful scientific solutions, helping to position UKCEH at the forefront of environmental innovation while supporting nature recovery and sustainable economic growth.

What we're looking for

This is a business development role first. We are looking for someone who knows how to originate, develop and close commercial work in a technical or B2B environment, for example in environmental consultancy, geospatial or data products, ESG, carbon or natural capital markets. You will also bring a good working knowledge of nature finance and the frameworks shaping it, and the curiosity to keep deepening it. You won't need to be the technical expert: you will work alongside UKCEH's in-house nature finance scientists and data specialists, who provide the scientific depth.

Your priorities in the first 12 to 18 months

Nature finance is a young market, and we expect income to build over time. In your first 12 to 18 months, your priorities will be to:

• Identify and take a number of priority UKCEH offers to market, such as monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) services for nature markets and high-resolution land cover data products.
• Build a qualified pipeline of opportunities with corporates, financial institutions, nature market developers and government.
• Develop and manage strategic partnerships, coordinating UKCEH's offer across teams.

Your main responsibilities will include:

Strategic external representation & market positioning

• Act as UKCEH's lead business development representative in nature finance and biodiversity markets, engaging senior stakeholders across financial institutions, corporates, government, NGOs and market developers.
• Represent UKCEH at conferences, working groups, investor forums and client meetings to raise profile and generate commercial opportunities.
• Build and maintain a strategic network across sustainability, ESG, finance, investment and nature market sectors.
• Stay informed on emerging developments and opportunities including TNFD, SBTN, Biodiversity Net Gain, biodiversity credits and nature-based solutions investment.
• Provide market intelligence and strategic insight to support UKCEH's commercial and scientific planning.

Commercial Pipeline Ownership & Income Generation

• Own and manage a commercial pipeline spanning contract research, strategic partnerships, advisory services, data products and collaborative programmes.
• Identify, develop and convert opportunities into commercial agreements and income.
• Work towards agreed pipeline and income targets, which will build as the market matures, providing regular pipeline forecasts and progress updates to senior leaders.
• Develop compelling commercial propositions that align market needs with UKCEH's scientific expertise.

Shaping Commercial Deals & Partnership Agreements

• Lead commercial discussions with partners and clients, agreeing the scope, value and commercial shape of each opportunity, and develop pricing with Finance colleagues.
• Support the development of commercial proposals, bids and partnership opportunities aligned to organisational priorities.
• Assess opportunities with sound judgement, ensuring alignment with UKCEH's values, scientific integrity and reputation.
• Work with Licensing & IPR and Contracts colleagues, who lead on agreement drafting, IP and licensing terms and contract management, to secure agreements that deliver commercial value while protecting UKCEH's independence and credibility.

Strategic Partnership Development

• Build and strengthen long-term relationships with corporates, financial institutions, government organisations and nature market stakeholders.
• Act as lead relationship manager for key accounts, ensuring a coordinated and high-quality experience across UKCEH.
• Identify opportunities for co-funded programmes, commercial partnerships and wider income generation.
• Collaborate with fundraising and business development colleagues to maximise strategic opportunities.

Cross-UKCEH Commercial Coordination

• Coordinate commercial activity across teams, ensuring a consistent approach to the nature finance market.
• Contribute to business development and pipeline discussions, supporting collaboration across commercial and fundraising teams.
• Maintain accurate records of commercial activity and stakeholder engagement within UKCEH's CRM systems.
• Contribute commercial insight and market intelligence to science area leadership and organisational strategy development.

Who you'll work with

You won't be doing this alone. You will lead customer engagement, opportunity development and the commercial relationship with each client, from first conversation to long-term account. Specialist teams across UKCEH will work alongside you:

• Licensing & IPR lead on agreement drafting, IP and licensing terms, and contract management after the deal. You agree the commercial shape of each deal with them.
• Finance work with you to develop pricing and costing, and manage invoicing and income.
• Contracts review and approve agreements and manage governance sign-off.
• The Project Management Office supports mobilisation and delivery once work is won.
• Fundraising lead on philanthropic opportunities, and you hand over where a corporate relationship has that potential.
• Business Development colleagues across UKCEH coordinate the wider income pipeline, so that UKCEH presents a joined-up offer.
• UKCEH scientists, including our nature finance scientists and data specialists, provide the scientific depth behind every proposition.

Qualifications and Experience:

• A proven track record of originating, developing and closing commercial work in a technical or B2B environment (for example environmental consultancy, geospatial or data products, ESG, carbon or natural capital markets), with evidence of generating income or partnership value.
• A good working knowledge of the nature finance landscape and how organisations are responding to it, including frameworks and markets such as TNFD, SBTN, Biodiversity Net Gain, biodiversity credits and nature-based solutions.
• Experience managing a commercial pipeline and building long-term client or partner relationships.
• Experience working with or selling the work of scientific, research or technical specialists, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling commercial propositions.
• Excellent relationship-building, influencing and stakeholder management skills, with the credibility to engage senior leaders across business, finance, policy and scientific communities.
• Strong commercial acumen, negotiation skills, and the ability to identify opportunities that align with organisational goals and values.
• Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing, bid development and presenting to senior audiences.

It would be great if you also have:

• An established network in nature finance, green finance, corporate sustainability or land use investment.
• Experience of public sector grant bids or match-funded programmes.

What we offer

At UKCEH, we recognise your dedication and provide a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you both at work and at home. When you join us, you'll benefit from:

• Generous annual leave - 27 days (rising to 29 days after 5 years) + 3 days for Christmas closure

• 10% employer pension contribution

• Financial protection through life assurance and income protection

• Enhanced family-friendly policies

• Flexible and hybrid working options (depending on your role)

• Lifestyle perks including dental, gym, retail and cycling discounts

• A commitment to wellbeing, supported by a range of internal initiatives

• Employee Assistance Programme and health benefits, including 24/7 support with remote GP access, mental health, physiotherapy and lifestyle services

• Peer recognition and rewards that celebrate your contribution

• Salary sacrifice agreement benefits including Electric & Plug-in Hybrid vehicle and Cycle2Work schemes

• Interest-free annual travel season ticket loans (terms apply)

How to apply and what happens next

If you're interested in this role, we'd love to hear from you. You'll be directed to our Workday portal where you'll create an account and upload your CV and a cover letter (approx. 8 mins). Your responses are an important part of our assessment process, so please take the time to complete them thoughtfully:

• A cover letter: Use clear, concise examples that demonstrate your achievements, relevant experience, skills and your motivation for joining UKCEH. Please include one example of a commercial opportunity you originated and closed, and what you learned from it.

• Once submitted, our panel will review your application, and please be assured that we are committed to providing an outcome for all applicants, regardless of the result.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

At UKCEH, we believe everyone should feel welcome and able to be themselves at work. We warmly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and identities. As a Disability Confident employer, we're happy to support you with any adjustments you may need throughout the recruitment process.

Please note: unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role and this does not qualify for endorsement to support a Global Talent Visa application. If you are considering pursuing self-sponsorship, please indicate this in your application so we can take it into account during the recruitment process.

If we've just described you, we'd love to meet. Apply now.

title: Social Worker
description:
Herefordshire Council,

About The Role

Job Title: Social Worker Advert - Young Adults Team

Hours: 37

Salary: HC08

Contract: Permanent

Closing date: 13/11/2026

Interview date: TBC

The Role

Are you passionate about helping young adults build confident, independent futures? Herefordshire Community Wellbeing is looking for an enthusiastic, professionally confident Social Worker to join our welcoming and supportive Young Adults Team. The team works with young people from the age of 16 who have an active Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and are likely to require Adult Social Care support beyond the age of 18, supporting effective preparation for adulthood and transition planning.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference at a pivotal point in people’s lives. You will work alongside young adults as they move into adulthood, helping them recognise their strengths, shape their goals and achieve greater choice, control and independence. You will join a team that values fresh ideas, reflective practice, professional curiosity and positive outcomes.

What will you be doing?

No two days will be the same. You will work creatively with young adults who have a range of care and support needs, which may include learning disabilities, physical disabilities, mental health needs and safeguarding concerns. By building trusted relationships with young adults, families, carers and partner agencies, you will help turn aspirations into practical, sustainable plans for adulthood. A significant part of your role will be to attend and contribute to annual Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) reviews with education providers from the age of 16, gathering relevant information, identifying likely care and support needs and helping to coordinate timely preparation for adulthood. You will undertake strengths-based assessments under the Care Act 2014 where appropriate and support coordinated planning for young people likely to require Adult Social Care support beyond the age of 18.

You will complete person-centred, strengths-based assessments under the Care Act 2014, alongside care and support planning, reviews and safeguarding work. We will support you to grow your confidence, deepen your specialist knowledge and continue developing as a skilled and reflective practitioner.

You will bring energy, sound professional judgement and a genuine commitment to personalised, outcome-focused practice. You will balance young adults’ views and aspirations with proportionate risk management and legal duties, while making creative use of family, community and universal resources. If you enjoy collaborative practice, thoughtful problem-solving and seeing young adults move towards the lives they want, we would love to hear from you.

Herefordshire is a rural county, and the ability to travel across the county is essential to the post.

About You

As a Social Worker in the Young Adults Team, you will have the opportunity to:

• Hold a recognised Social Work qualification.
• Be registered with Social Work England.
• Demonstrate knowledge of strengths-based practice and assessment under the Care Act 2014.
• Be able to communicate effectively with young adults, families, carers and professionals.
• Be able to undertake person-centred, strengths-based assessments under the Care Act 2014, alongside outcome-focused care and support planning and review.

Understand the purpose of EHCPs and be able to contribute clear social care information to annual reviews, preparation-for-adulthood planning and strengths-based assessments under the Care Act 2014.

Use your professional judgement to promote independence, manage risk and safeguard young adults.

Bring young people, families, education providers, health colleagues, Children’s Services and Adult Social Care together to contribute effectively to EHCP annual reviews and create coordinated, timely transition plans.

We Offer

A competitive salary, holiday entitlement, and access to our contributory pension and staff benefits scheme, which includes:

• Salary and any welcome payment will be confirmed in the published vacancy details.
• Enrolment in the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS)
• Career progression: clear pathways to progress
• Annual Leave: 31 days’ annual leave (pro rata) plus bank holidays. You can also purchase an additional 10 days per annum during the request period
• Flexible working: including the potential for job-sharing, part-time hours and agile working.
• Employee Assistance Programme: 24/7 access to support and counselling
• Payment of professional membership fees (based on role requirements)
• Pick your perks – our benefits include access to a range of retail, leisure, holiday and health benefits. This includes savings, cash back and discounts.

Why Choose Us?

We're proud and excited to unveil our new recruitment video, a celebration of Herefordshire's people, places, and purpose. Set in the heart of England and filled with pride, compassion and possibility, the video brings to life what it means to work somewhere you truly belong.

At Herefordshire Council, every role matters and every person makes a real difference for our communities. We’re a team where people feel valued, supported and empowered to grow together.

You will probably have heard a lot about how beautiful it is in terms of countryside and open spaces (and it is!) but there is so much more going on here, including world-class cultural assets like the Mappa Mundi, vibrant theatres and a thriving food and drink sector. One of Herefordshire’s biggest assets is the strong and diverse communities. Our Talk Community approach brings that together supporting people to help themselves, encouraging them to help their communities and identifying how communities can help individuals.

Our ambitious transformation programme aims to further build on this to offer an all-age approach. We’re excited about the potential of what we can achieve for the benefit of all residents of Herefordshire, stronger together and building brighter futures.

Don’t meet all parts of the job description?

Herefordshire Council is committed to strengthening a diverse and inclusive work environment which reflects the communities of Herefordshire. If you are looking at the next stage of your career and have a broad base of fieldwork experience, we can provide supportive and welcoming opportunities to help you develop your professional, management & supervisory skills.

Reasonable Adjustments

Our recruitment process runs in partnership with Hoople Resourcing. If you require any reasonable adjustments or alternative methods for the online application process, please contact the resourcing team by email: enquiries@hoopleresourcing.co.uk.

Creating an inclusive workplace

We encourage our employees to feel empowered and to use their voices to help embrace diversity, promote inclusivity and shape our organisation. We have eight employee network groups, collectives of colleagues who often share identities, life experiences or cultures and offer support and community. They also play an important role in strengthening the voices of employees at Herefordshire Council. Embedded in the Council's values is a commitment to listen to people's views and needs.

For more information on our Employee Network Groups please view our dedicated recruitment website: www.spiritofherefordshire.com.

Commitments, Covenants and Statutory Obligations

The following candidates will be interviewed if they meet the essential criteria for the post they are applying for:

• Those who indicate that they have a disability. This is part of our commitment to the “Disability Confident” scheme.
• Those who indicate in their application that they are an Armed Forces Veteran or Reservist. This is part of our pledge to support the Armed Forces Covenant.
• Those who indicate in their application that they are a Herefordshire care leaver. This is part of our commitment to supporting young people leaving our care.

We take our commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults seriously and expect all of our staff, visitors and volunteers to share in this commitment.

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children & young people and vulnerable adults. If you are offered this position, it will be subject to a Disclosure and Barring Service check.

How To Apply

To apply for a position, please upload an up-to-date CV and complete the application form demonstrating your experience, skills and abilities for the role.

For more information or to arrange an informal discussion about the role, please contact: (Richard Clarke, Team Manager. 01432 383604).

Be sure to include reference to the job description and person specification or role profile! If you are successfully shortlisted, Hoople Resourcing will contact you via email to arrange your interview and/or assessment. They will confirm the date, time and location of your interview, so please keep an eye on your email inbox - check your spam/ junk folder too. Good luck, we’re looking forward to meeting you!

title: Social Worker - Family Support Team x  2
description:
At Bath & North East Somerset Council we have one overriding purpose to improve people’s lives.

Role

This role is eligible for a £2,000 Retention Payment (prorata for parttime roles). To recognise and reward commitment, a £2,000 retention payment is available. This will be paid in two instalments:

• £1,000 after completing 12 months of service
• £500 after completing 18 months of service
• £500 after completing 24 months of service

If your passion is around collaborative work with families, centred on building relationships in order to help families develop resilience and make changes for their children, then we are the Local Authority for you. Working with families to keep children at home wherever possible, our dynamic teams work with families from point of contact through to long term support and intervention. Our practice model is underpinned by relationship-based, systemic approaches to facilitate change, alongside trauma informed practice.

Bath and North East Somerset Children’s Social Care are an innovative small Local Authority focused on therapeutic assessment and support. Rated Good by OFSTED, with continued vision and drive to improve further.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced qualified Social Worker to join one of our Family Support Teams, within the Safeguarding Outcomes Service. We are committed to being a dynamic and creative Local Authority, working hard to think differently about how we approach our work with families. We are deeply committed to providing tailored high-quality services and well thought out interventions to families to keep children safe. Our practice is values-driven with a strong ethos of child-focussed interventions.

About The Role

You will work in partnership with an enthusiastic hub consisting of a Team Manager, Deputy Team Managers, Senior Social Work Practitioners, qualified professional Social Workers, Family Support Practitioners and Administrative staff.

This rewarding role will see you responding to, co-ordinating and delivering a range of social care services to children, young people and families in the Bath and North East Somerset area for children subject to Child in Need Plans, Child Protection Plans, Children in Care, and children subject to legal proceedings. The role will include undertaking single assessments and section 47 child protection investigations. We work closely with our colleagues across the service and have established partnerships with agencies across health, education, support services and adult services to ensure we can respond as effectively as possible to the needs of children, young people, and their families.

We work closely with our Family Support Plus team who deliver extensive Family Group Conferences to utilise resources and support within families to keep children safe, as well as tailored interventions including the New Way domestic abuse service.

About You

The post holder will manage their own caseload, which will include children and families with complex needs. You will be able to evidence a strong ability to analyse information and formulate outcome focused plans for children and families. Applicants must be confident in writing professional assessments/reports as well as presenting their evidence verbally. Applicants need to have very strong organisational skills to manage and prioritise their work effectively and in a timely way and will be committed to working as part of a team to support colleagues in delivering optimum services to children and families.

We are seeking applications from workers who have relevant experience and a specific interest in this area of work and are looking to enhance and further develop their skills and contribute to service development for vulnerable children.

You Can Expect

• A comprehensive induction
• Managed caseload; supporting children in need, children subject to child protection plans, and children protected through legal proceedings
• Regular supervision at a minimum of monthly one to one

title: Experienced Social Worker - Children's Services
description:
Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council,

Experienced Social Worker

Teams: Various

Salary up to £49,817 per year

Hours: Permanent full-time, Monday to Friday with flexible working

Following our recent Ofsted Good judgement, there has never been a better time to join Solihull Children's Services. With competitive salaries up to £49,817, a supportive permanent leadership team and flexible working arrangements, you'll be part of a service committed to achieving the best outcomes for children and families.

About The Role

This is an exciting opportunity to join Solihull Children's Services as we continue to develop our new Family Help model, bringing together social workers, family support workers and partner agencies to provide joined-up, relationship-based support for children and families.

We are looking for experienced Social Workers who are respectful, kind and passionate about making a positive difference to the lives of vulnerable children, young people and their families. Working within one of our Family Help Teams, you will undertake assessments, support children and families through change, and help achieve positive outcomes.

Solihull is a local authority that is big enough to make a difference, but small enough to care. With manageable caseloads, supportive managers and a stable, experienced workforce, we offer an environment where social workers can focus on what matters most: building strong relationships with children and families and delivering high-quality practice.

These roles will be based in our modern offices in Chelmunds Place and the Bluebell Centre in Chelmsley Wood, Solihull.

Our Offer to You

• Competitive Salaries - Earn one of the highest salaries (within the top three) in the region - up to £49,817 per annum (as confirmed by an independent pay analysis of 13 local authorities across the West Midlands).
• Manageable workloads – allowing you the time to give dedicated support where it is needed.
• Guaranteed regular supervision, to ensure you feel supported and are on the right track.
• Local government pension – Up to 6.8% (subject to annual review/change) section contribution.
• Generous annual leave - 25 days rising to 30 days after five years’ service and the opportunity to buy up to 10 days’ additional leave per year.
• Flexible working – including a flexi time scheme and hybrid working.
• Professional development - High quality year-round training and coaching and in house academic programmes (Practice Education Award) via our Children's Social Care Academy (in partnership with Bournemouth University)
• Clear career pathways through to Advanced Practitioner, specialist roles and leadership and management.
• Employee Assistance Programme – 24/7 access to independent, free and confidential support and advice
• Training on and use of Beam Notes (AI) - to enable you to spend more time working directly with our children, young people and their families.
• Relocation Package – up to £6,500 towards the cost of moving house (terms and conditions apply).

About You

Successful applicants will be committed to delivering a high-quality, transparent service and ensuring the wellbeing of children, young people and their families in Solihull. You will also have:

• A professional Social Worker qualification and current Social Work England registration
• Significant post qualifying experience
• A solution-focussed approach
• A sound knowledge of current national and regional social work policies/practices and relevant childcare legislation
• A driving licence and own your own vehicle (this is an essential car user post due to the demands of the job). For disabled applicants, reasonable adjustments will be made where required.

About Us

At Solihull, children and young people are at the heart of everything we do. We are launching eight new Family Help Teams, bringing together skilled professionals to provide timely, relationship-based support that improves outcomes for children and families. Our Family Help Teams are pivotal to the delivery of the national reforms locally, enabling children and families to access more coordinated support from one team around the family.

Each Family Help Team consists of five Social Workers, three Family Support Workers, an Advanced Practitioner and a Team Manager, creating the capacity and expertise needed to deliver meaningful interventions. Teams receive support from a multi-agency Partnership Hub, which includes Domestic Abuse services (including an Independent Domestic Violence Advisor and perpetrator offer), Edge of Care, Family Group Conferencing, Youth Justice, Harm Outside the Home, Education inclusion, Educational Psychology, Housing and the Department for Work and Pensions. Together, we provide coordinated support that helps families build on their strengths and achieve lasting change.

Family Help Teams work with children and families from the point of referral through assessment and intervention, undertaking Section 17 and Section 47 assessments and working alongside families on Family Help and Child Protection plans. Teams operate a one-week-in-eight duty rota, while a specialist Court Team undertakes the majority of public law and some private law work. With average caseloads of 18 children, a highly stable workforce and many agency workers choosing to become permanent employees, our social workers have the capacity to build meaningful relationships with families and deliver lasting change

For more information about the many benefits of working for Solihull, our teams or to see our other vacancies, please click here.

title: Mobile Vehicle Technician - Oldham
description:
Join the RAC as a Mobile Vehicle Technician in our SMR Division - a new era of mobile repair.

• A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000
• A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities
• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Oldham / Bury cluster, covering areas like Oldham, Bury, Rochdale, Middleton, Chadderton, Failsworth, Whitefield, Prestwich, Radcliffe, Heywood, Ramsbottom. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability
• Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000. It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward.
• Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings.
• Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays. We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments.
• Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term.
• Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16+, offering reassurance whenever you need it.
• Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success.

Who thrives here?You’re more than just great with tools - you’re great with people. Our Mobile Mechanics are the face of the RAC: working on driveways, in car parks, speaking directly with members, and providing reassurance, clarity and high-quality service.

You enjoy independence, problem solving and real variety - each job is different. From servicing and diagnostics to in depth repairs and reporting, you’re hands-on, adaptable and confident making decisions on the spot.

You take pride in using your technical ability to genuinely help people and keep them moving.

The role is ideal if you want:✔ Independence in a mobile role

✔ The stability and support of a trusted national organisation

✔ Ongoing development, including future EV and diagnostic skills

✔ A role where giving members complete peace of mind is simply part of what you do

We’re the RACAt the RAC, we don’t stand still. With over 125 years of history and 12.5 million members, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

Our culture reflects that ambition - backed by a 4.5-star Glassdoor rating, our people know we’re serious about career growth, recognition, and support.

We celebrate individuality and champion every voice. As an equal opportunities' employer, we welcome people from all backgrounds and walks of life - it’s what sets us apart and drives us forward.
