description:
Job Overview

Wrexham and Flintshire CAMHS are excited to be recruiting to multiple full and part time CAMHS Practitioner posts, to support the work of the GP In-Reach Team. We are focused on expanding our support to children, young people and their families at an early stage, to promote wellbeing and prevent the development of significant mental health difficulties. Our vision is to enhance and develop early intervention provision by increasing access to help at the right time, in the right place, from the right people.

You will be joining a skilled team of Senior Community CAMHS Practitioners across Wrexham and Flintshire who are leading on this work and have begun developing this vision; initially through working with GP practices.

We are looking for people who are confident in their skills and knowledge of children and young people’s mental health and who can communicate this effectively to others. You will primarily offer brief assessment, advice and intervention to children and young people who access their GP for support with emotional and mental health difficulties. Other duties will include offering consultation and advice to GPs and Practice staff, and supporting senior colleagues in the team with service developments, such as the delivery of training.

Main duties of the job

Applicants will need to be compliant with the professional requirements as determined by Mental Health Measure 2010 and should have a relevant professional and registered qualification relating to Health or Social Care (e.g. Clinical Psychology, Mental Health or Learning Disability Nursing, Occupational Therapy or Social work). Applicants should also be able to demonstrate a high level of competence, knowledge and skills (underpinned by knowledge of effective risk assessment and relevant evidence-based practice, which is crucial to this role).

Applicants should be able to demonstrate evidence of their clinical understanding and decision-making skills; be a committed team player with the ability to prioritise their own workload, and work well under pressure. Good IT skills are essential with confidence in Outlook, Word and Excel.

There may be some requirement to support weekend ward-based risk assessments as part of a rota.

title: Consultant in Emergency Medicine
description:
Job Overview

The Emergency Department (ED) was purpose built in 2014 and offers state of-the-art facilities. This was part of a new development at YGC called the Emergency Quadrant (EQ) which brings all Emergency and Acute Services together. The EQ houses the ED, Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC), a 24 bed Acute Medical Unit, Surgical Assessment Unit, Radiology services.

The ED sees a full case mix of undifferentiated emergencies encompassing all specialties including Major Trauma, Stroke, Cardiac, Vascular, ENT, Ophthalmology, Max Fax and Paediatrics.

The Department has also been undergoing a process of implementation of modern models of Emergency Care including streaming, ambulatory majors, and rapid assessment.

Main duties of the job

• Leading medical handovers and huddles
• Support the Nurse in Charge (NIC) to manage Emergency Department (ED) risk escalating ED capacity and safety concerns
• Being a point of clinical contact in ED for Senior Clinicians and Management
• Support the coordination of workforce resources within ED, including responding to short-notice staffing gaps and escalating workforce concerns to maintain safe service provision
• Using Symphony to proactively run the ED
• Focusing on patient safety risks, reviewing unwell patients, and seeing patients as needed
• Supporting the streaming of patients to Minor Injury Units (MIUs), Specialities or Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) where appropriate
• Anticipating and intervening with unexpected issues, e.g., health and safety risks

Working for our organisation

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales’s largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

title: Associate / Senior Associate Mechanical Engineer (Data Centres and Mission Critical)
description:
About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

We have an exciting opportunity for an Associate / Senior Associate Mechanical Engineer to join our Data Centre & Mission Critical (MCDC) team at Hoare Lea.

Data centres are central to the modern economy and the technology that powers them is evolving rapidly. Our Mission Critical team helps clients navigate these changing requirements. At Hoare Lea you’ll gain a truly unique experience working across the full spectrum of the data-centre sector — from early-stage site appraisal, master planning and feasibility studies through detailed plant and HVAC design, live plant upgrades, test-fits, commissioning and operational optimisation.

You’ll work across close-control environments, data halls, live plant replacement and refurbishment, critical engineering and due-diligence reviews of existing facilities. Projects span mainly in UK, but also across Ireland and Europe.

You will join a collaborative, knowledgeable and highly engaged team with a positive, supportive and flexible culture. Working alongside the Project Leader, you will engage directly with clients, develop designs and produce reports, specifications and guidance, and support testing and commissioning activities to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes.

In This Key And Varied Role You Will

• Lead mechanical design delivery for data centre and mission-critical projects.
• Act as a senior client-facing engineer across design teams and stakeholders.
• Prepare and review specifications, reports and technical deliverables.
• Support strategic site appraisals, feasibility, masterplanning and test-fit studies.
• Oversee plant design, commissioning, handover and operational optimisation.
• Support fee, resource and project delivery management.
• Mentor and develop engineers, apprentices and graduates.

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

• Proven experience delivering mission critical and data centre projects.
• Strong knowledge of HVAC, chilled water and refrigerant systems, cooling plant, air distribution and heat rejection.
• Experience with Revit, BIM workflows and AutoCAD.
• Strong client-facing consultancy experience.
• Excellent technical judgement and a collaborative mindset.
• Experience mentoring and supporting others.

Desired Specialist Experience

• Mission-critical and data centre mechanical engineering across new-build, live operational upgrades, technical due diligence, feasibility studies and test-fits.
• Large-scale, multi-megawatt data centre developments.
• Hyperscale, colocation and enterprise/research environments.
• Early-stage site appraisal, masterplanning and test-fit studies.
• Cooling infrastructure and heat-rejection options.
• Resilience and uptime design thinking.
• High-density and AI-ready cooling.
• Live operational environments and phased upgrades.
• Campus-scale developments and multidisciplinary coordination.
• Energy efficiency and sustainability in mission-critical design.
• Experience working across the UK; international experience is desirable.

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application, or for further information please contact jessicamartin@hoarelea.com.

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.

Adjustments and accommodations

If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to help you participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence or anything else) please let us know.

We have updated our terms and conditions for candidates, click here to find out more.

description:
Conveyancing Solicitor (NQ–3 PQE)

Location: St Albans, Hertfordshire

Practice Area: Residential Property

Job Type: Permanent, Full-Time

The Opportunity

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a Conveyancing Solicitor (NQ–5 PQE) to join a busy, growing and well-established residential property team based in St Albans, Hertfordshire

This role would suit a newly qualified or junior Solicitor looking to develop their career within a supportive, high-performing environment, with the opportunity to take ownership of their own caseload and gain further exposure to a broad range of residential property transactions.

We are particularly keen to speak with candidates who have genuine hands-on experience managing and progressing their own conveyancing matters, rather than solely providing support to more senior fee earners.

Key Responsibilities

• Manage a caseload of residential conveyancing transactions from initial instruction through to exchange and completion.
• Handle freehold and leasehold sales and purchases.
• Review title documentation, searches, contracts and property information.
• Raise and respond to enquiries, identifying and resolving potential issues.
• Draft contracts, reports on title, completion statements and associated documentation.
• Liaise with clients, estate agents, lenders, brokers and other legal professionals.
• Advise clients throughout the conveyancing process, providing clear, commercially focused advice.
• Manage exchange, completion and relevant post-completion formalities, including SDLT and registration requirements.
• Maintain accurate files and ensure compliance with regulatory and internal procedures.
• Proactively progress transactions, manage deadlines and deliver excellent client service.

About You

To be considered, you will ideally have:

• Qualified Solicitor status in England & Wales, with NQ–5 years PQE.
• Practical residential conveyancing experience gained during training and/or post-qualification.
• Direct experience handling and progressing your own conveyancing files.
• A sound understanding of residential sales and purchases, including freehold and leasehold transactions.
• Confidence dealing directly with clients, lenders, estate agents and other solicitors.
• The ability to identify issues, resolve enquiries and progress matters efficiently.
• Strong drafting, communication and organisational skills.
• A proactive, commercially aware and client-focused approach.
• The ability to manage competing priorities and work independently while contributing to a wider team.

Experience with new-build transactions, remortgages, transfers of equity, shared ownership or high-volume caseloads would be advantageous but is not essential.

What We're Looking For

The key requirement is genuine fee-earning conveyancing experience.

We are looking for someone who has taken meaningful responsibility for progressing their own matters, including client communication, dealing with enquiries and working towards exchange and completion.

Applications from newly qualified Solicitors are welcomed, provided they can demonstrate substantial hands-on experience gained during a residential conveyancing seat.

This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious junior Solicitor who enjoys client contact, takes ownership of their work and wants to continue developing their technical expertise within a busy residential property team.

Interested?

If you're a Residential Conveyancing Solicitor looking for your next opportunity in St Albans, Hertfordshire , we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or get in touch for a confidential discussion about the role.

• 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

Where you’ll work

You’ll be part of the Chichester cluster, covering areas like Portsmouth, Havant, Waterlooville, Fareham, Gosport, Emsworth. You’ll be out on the road in your local area, working through a clearly planned schedule of appointments - no reactive callouts, just organised, pre‑booked work where you can focus on doing the job properly.

A Different Kind of RAC Role: Welcome to SMR

The RAC is known for roadside rescue - but this isn’t that.

Our Service, Maintenance & Repair (SMR) division is a newer, fast-growing part of the RAC, built to deliver planned, structured repair and servicing directly to members - from their driveway to their workplace car park.

There are no emergency callouts, no unpredictable shift patterns and no roadside recoveries. Instead, you’ll work through a scheduled list of jobs, with the time, tools and support you need to do quality work.

What To Expect

Your day starts with a clear digital schedule. Each job is pre‑booked, with the member expecting you. You’ll carry out:

• Routine servicing
• Diagnostics using advanced mobile equipment
• In‑depth repairs you’d normally complete in a workshop
• Member advice and recommendations based on your inspection
• Vehicle safety checks aligned to RAC standards

And because SMR is structured, you’re not reacting to breakdowns - you’re delivering planned work that you can prepare for.

From day one, you’ll have everything you need: a fully equipped RAC van, fuel card, uniform, full tool set and advanced diagnostics. You’ll use your technical skill and problem‑solving ability to get people moving again; safely, quickly and confidently.

Why SMR is different (and why techs love it)

• Planned appointments instead of emergency responses
• Consistent workflow instead of unpredictable demands
• In‑depth repairs, not roadside temporary fixes
• Time to do the job properly, with support and parts ordering built in
• Clear schedules using RAC’s mobile service platform

It’s the ideal role for techs who want variety and independence without the reactive nature of Patrol.

What You’ll Need...

Either:

NVQ Level 2 qualification in Light Vehicle Maintenance (or equivalent) with 2+ years’ experience

or

5+ years’ experience as a Vehicle Technician/Mechanic

and

A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points

No CV required when you apply and it takes just 5 minutes - it's easier than ever to start your journey with us.

As a Mobile Mechanic at the RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile:

• Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime. A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday-Saturday availability (8am-8pm), offers flexibility and stability
• Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000. It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward.
• Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings.
• Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays. We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments.
• Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term.
• Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16+, offering reassurance whenever you need it.
• Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success.

Who thrives here?You’re more than just great with tools - you’re great with people. Our Mobile Mechanics are the face of the RAC: working on driveways, in car parks, speaking directly with members, and providing reassurance, clarity and high-quality service.

You enjoy independence, problem solving and real variety - each job is different. From servicing and diagnostics to in depth repairs and reporting, you’re hands-on, adaptable and confident making decisions on the spot.

You take pride in using your technical ability to genuinely help people and keep them moving.

The role is ideal if you want:✔ Independence in a mobile role

✔ The stability and support of a trusted national organisation

✔ Ongoing development, including future EV and diagnostic skills

✔ A role where giving members complete peace of mind is simply part of what you do

We’re the RACAt the RAC, we don’t stand still. With over 125 years of history and 12.5 million members, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

Our culture reflects that ambition - backed by a 4.5-star Glassdoor rating, our people know we’re serious about career growth, recognition, and support.

We celebrate individuality and champion every voice. As an equal opportunities' employer, we welcome people from all backgrounds and walks of life - it’s what sets us apart and drives us forward.

title: Support Worker
description:
Up to £42,775+ earning potential | 4 on 4 off shift pattern | Career Progression and funded qualifications | North East Based

At Nova Care Group, we know that supporting a young person through crisis and complexity takes more than experience on paper.

It takes patience, resilience, the ability to stay calm when things are difficult, build trust when trust doesn't come easily and look beyond behaviour to understand what might be driving it.

We know this because our organisation was founded on lived experience. We've seen first hand how much difference the right people, at the right time, can make in a young person's life.

Now we're looking for people who want to make that difference too.

The role

We want to be honest with you, this isn't always an easy job but it will always make a difference.

The young people we support have experienced significant challenges in their lives and often communicate their experiences through behaviours such as aggression, absconding, sexualised behaviours, self-harm, criminalisation or withdrawing from others.

Your role is to stay calm, consistent and compassionate. To set clear boundaries, build trust and look beyond the behaviour to understand what a young person may be experiencing.

There will be challenging times, difficult conversations and times when progress feels slow. Then there are the moments that make it all worthwhile.

Seeing a young person begin to trust you, watching them manage something they couldn't before, seeing their confidence grow, their behaviour stabilise or taking another step towards independence.

Requirements For Our Support Workers

If you've worked in a demanding environment such as care, education, prison service, police, emergency services, armed forces, security, hospitality, retail or another role where you've had to remain calm under pressure, you'll already have many of the skills we're looking for. You’ll be:

• Fully flexible and able to work and travel across the North East
• Able to work 12 hours shifts, covering days, waking nights and sleep in shifts.
• In possession of a Full UK Driving licence and right to work in the UK (we are not able to offer sponsorship)

What You'll Receive

• £30,000£32,000 basic salary
• Shift enhancements with earning potential of £42,775+
• A 4 on 4 off shift pattern, giving you regular blocks of time away from work
• Enhanced annual leave, increasing with length of service
• Private healthcare cover
• Team bonus opportunities
• Fully funded Level 3 and Level 4 NVQ qualifications
• Clear career and progression pathways
• Paid sick leave
• Company pension scheme
• Refer a friend scheme
• Blue Light discounts

Experience working with young people is helpful, but it's not essential. We'll provide the training and support you need to develop in the role.

Nova Care Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of the young people we support. This role is subject to safer recruitment checks, including an enhanced DBS, employment history and reference checks.

title: Sales Advisor

There is an exciting opportunity to join Bellway, one of the UK's largest house builders. Our Scotland West Division is looking to recruit a Sales Advisor to join the Division's Sales team.

title: Accountants Payable Assistant
description:
Be a part of something bigger...

Our Story

Be a part of something bigger...

Radar Healthcare is dedicated to improving patient safety by bringing together the expertise of healthcare professionals and the power of intuitive software. Our innovative platform has been developed in partnership with industry experts to ensure organisations always meet regulatory standards – making it easier than ever for healthcare providers to deliver top-quality care to their patients.

We’re on a mission to become a world-leading health-tech pioneer, and we know that we can only achieve this with the help of talented individuals like you. If you’re passionate about improving healthcare outcomes and want to work in a team of like-minded individuals, we invite you to join us on our journey.

So if you’re up for an exciting challenge and want to be part of a team that’s making a real impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Our Values

At Radar Healthcare, we are all proud of our values-led, open, supportive and inclusive culture. It's just as important that anyone joining our friendly team share the same values as us, to ensure we're all on the same page from day one, so we're looking for people who feel aligned to the following:

🤝🏽 Customer focused with a partnership approach

📖 Open, honest and transparent

🧠 Innovative

🫶🏼 Ethical, trustworthy and caring

Our People & Culture

At Radar Healthcare, we understand and celebrate the fact that our people are our best assets! We are proud to showcase our diverse and passionate talent that encapsulates our vision, purpose and values in our shared mission of innovation in healthcare. We’re an ambitious but caring team, and so supporting our colleagues and partners is always a top priority. Not to mention, we’re not all work and no play – we love getting together to celebrate our achievements together in various settings, whether it be our winter and summer socials, our people-led full company days, team get togethers or simply just interacting and supporting one another over coffee breaks either remotely or in person at our amazing Leeds office.

"We're also super proud to be Great Place to Work-Certified, based on outstanding feedback directly from our team earlier this year, with 91% of the team agreeing that they "would strongly endorse my company to friends and family as a great place to work" Not to mention Radar Healthcare has been named one of the UK’s Top 100 Companies to Work For 2025, one of the Top 20 Tech Companies to Work For, and has received a Two Star Accreditation from Best Companies, recognising ‘Outstanding’ levels of workplace engagement."" 🫶🏼

The Opportunity

Radar Healthcare's new ⭐Accounts Payable Assistant ⭐

To support the Finance team in managing the company’s purchase ledger operations while gaining practical experience and knowledge of financial processes within the health tech sector. The role supports accurate invoice and expense processing, supplier payments, account maintenance, financial record-keeping, reporting and compliance, while developing capability in financial systems, data analysis and process improvement.

What you’ll be doing to make a difference:

Invoice and Expense Processing

• Receive, verify and code supplier invoices accurately.
• Manage the employee expenses process from start to finish.
• Enter invoice data accurately into the financial system.
• Match invoices with purchase orders and goods received notes.

Payment Management

• Prepare payment runs.
• Schedule and process supplier payments.
• Maintain accurate records of payments made and outstanding.

Supplier Account Maintenance

• Reconcile supplier statements with internal records.
• Resolve discrepancies and queries with suppliers.
• Maintain up-to-date supplier information.
• Complete new vendor verification.

Financial Record-Keeping and Banking

• Maintain the purchase ledger system and organise financial documents.
• Prepare reports on accounts payable status and ageing.
• Enter bank transactions and complete bank reconciliations.
• Support payment run management.

Payroll, Data Analysis and Reporting

• Process payroll in accordance with third-party instructions.
• Compile data for purchase ledger reports and analyse spending patterns and supplier performance.
• Prepare financial summaries for management review.

Compliance and Process Improvement

• Assist in ensuring adherence to financial policies and procedures.
• Maintain records for audit purposes and support the team in staying current with relevant financial regulations.
• Identify and suggest improvements to purchase ledger processes.

Stakeholder Communication and Team Support

• Respond to supplier enquiries and prepare information for internal stakeholders.
• Monitor the accounts and purchases mailbox.
• Assist other Finance team members as required.
• Contribute to a positive and collaborative working environment.

Security and Quality Responsibilities:

• Protect the confidentiality, integrity and security of financial, supplier and employee information.
• Follow information security policies, access controls and approved methods for processing, storing and sharing data.
• Verify supplier and payment information and remain alert to phishing, fraud and suspicious requests, escalating concerns promptly.
• Maintain accurate records, follow documented controls and quality standards, and check work carefully before processing.
• Support audits, identify data quality improvements, escalate control failures and complete required security and data protection training.

Your journey so far...

• Ability to work with numbers and perform simple calculations accurately.
• Familiarity with basic office software, particularly Microsoft Excel.
• Basic understanding of financial concepts such as invoices, purchase orders and credit notes.
• Demonstrable interest in finance and/or the healthtech sector.
• Strong attention to detail.
• Ability to communicate effectively with colleagues and suppliers.
• Ability to manage and prioritise tasks efficiently.
• Eagerness to learn and develop.
• Effective time management, with the ability to meet deadlines and manage multiple tasks.
• Problem-solving skills and the ability to identify and resolve straightforward discrepancies.
• Ability to work collaboratively within a Finance team.

Even better if you…

• Experience using Sage Intacct.

The Bigger Picture

Whilst we value professional experiences and qualifications, we’re committed to maintaining a culture of growth and development here at Radar Healthcare. We take into account each candidates demonstrable skillset, drive and ethos so even if you don’t feel 100% qualified for the role – we welcome you to connect with us. We’d love to hear from passionate candidates from all backgrounds that align themselves with our company values and are excited to make a difference in healthcare!

What we offer in return...

💰 A competitive salary of up to £27,000 per year, dependent on experience

💜 Values-led culture - we’re extremely proud of our culture. Learn more about what makes it special here

🏢 Flexible working – We believe in empowering our team to work in a way that suits them best. Whether you’re an early bird or prefer working from home most of the time, we trust you to get the job done around our core hours. We have a base expectation of 1 day per month in the office but outside of this, although we have a fantastic office in the heart of Leeds (complete with a rooftop bar for the summer months), the choice is yours!

🏝️ 25 days holiday (+ Bank holidays) continually increasing with service, plus the option to buy up to a week to suit whatever exotic adventures or big life events you have planned for the year ahead

🎂 Birthdays off and a surprise through the letterbox - we love to make a song and dance about every year around the sun!

🤝🏽 Charity leave – giving back is important to us, so we empower all our team members to support charity every year on company time

🧠 Mental healthcare - Face to face counselling support, an app, and an Employee Assistance Program and many colleagues trained in mental health first aid

👩🏾‍⚕️ Healthcare - Cover with Medicash, you get money back when you spend on health appointments e.g. physio, dental, optician, prescriptions, private GP + more

💛 Life cover – a pay-out of 3x your salary to support your beneficiaries if the worst happened

💐 Compassionate leave of up to 5 days time off if you lose a loved one

🤕 Paid sick leave - Enhanced sick pay after 6 months (increasing with service)

🍼 Enhanced family leave - Primary caregivers (maternity/adoption); 16 weeks full pay, 10 weeks half pay & secondary caregivers (paternity); 2 weeks full pay and another 2 weeks full pay to take in your new arrivals first year of life (once you have been with us for 1 year)

💵 Pension - We’re invested in your future, we contribute 3% of your salary to your pension pot, helping you save up for those golden years!

🚙Electric vehicle scheme - Save up to 60% on the cost of an Electric Car

👶Workplace Nursery Scheme - Save up to 41% on nursery fees while accessing a growing network of nursery partners across the UK

🚲Cycle, Tech & Home schemes - Save on home and tech purchases by spreading the cost through interest-free salary deductions, with access to products from leading retailers.

💻 Technology – Rest assured, we'll have a laptop all set up and ready for you on your first day. Additionally, in your first week, we’ll conduct a WFH risk assessment to ensure you have everything you need, including a second screen, keyboard, mouse, and any other goodies!

🐶 Dog friendly office

🎈 Socials – we get together as a full company at least four times per year, plus at least once a quarter in individual teams, too. Not including all the fun activities being planned by our newly formed social committee.

🧩 Discounts on cinema, vouchers, gym memberships, days out and much much more

✨ PLUS a monthly £36 allowance on our flexible benefits platform Radar Rewards to spend on whatever else you might be after (private medical insurance, dental insurance, critical illness cover, or upgrade any of the covers above) with the ability to top up from salary if desired. We’re all different, after all!

Accessibility

If you require any special considerations or adjustments to our application and interviewing process, please don't hesitate to let us know. We understand and celebrate the fact that every person that we connect with is different and therefore requires different starting points on their journey with us. If you have a medical condition or disability we are committed to ensuring that our process is inclusive and accessible for all, let us know how we can best support you.

Connect with us!

We'd love to hear from you! If this role isn't quite right for you but you feel like Radar Healthcare could be, click the Connect button on our careers site and we'll keep you in the loop of new opportunities as they arise. You can also find out more about our mission, values and culture by checking out our various channels:

🎧 Listen to Our What the HealthTech podcast

🔗 Connect with us on Linkedin

💚 Discover why Radar Healthcare is a fantastic place to work from our very own people on Glassdoor!

Connect with us on our journey and get to know the people who make us shine!

title: Head of Professional Services
description:
About Doherty Associates

Doherty Associates (DA) have delivered IT solutions for over 35 years to world-renowned, international clients. Our customers operate predominantly in the professional and financial services sector, including leading private equity and top tier law firms.

We are a Microsoft Solutions Partner with five designations, hold a Tier 1 Microsoft CSP relationship and are ISO27001 & ISO9001 accredited. Our services are built on the Microsoft cloud ecosystem, aligned to the NIST Cyber Security Framework, and focused on quality, security, and long term client outcomes.

About the role

Reporting to the COO, the Head of Professional Services is responsible for leading and evolving the Professional Services function, owning the end to end delivery of customer projects, ensuring they meet their expectations by delivering consistently, profitably, and to a high standard.

This is a senior leadership role, accountable for delivery governance, people leadership, commercial performance, and the continuous improvement of delivery capability. The Head of Professional Services will act as both a strategic leader and a senior point of engagement for customers and internal stakeholders.

The Head of Professional Service will hold an overall accountability for two critical business functions:

• the Project Management Office (PMO) that drives consistent governance, delivery discipline, and commercial control over our project portfolio; and
• the technical delivery teams responsible for designing and implementing customer IT solutions (primarily Microsoft cloud, modern workplace and core infrastructure services).

The Head of Professional Services will hold an overall accountability for solutions design and delivery, their quality, customer satisfaction, utilisation, margin performance, and the maturity of the approach to project and engineering delivery at scale.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Culture

• Be a visible, credible leader by modelling core behaviours and setting high standards for delivery excellence, both internally and externally.
• Build a supportive, inclusive, high-performance culture across PMO and technical delivery underpinned by setting clear expectations, disciplined operating routines, effective coaching, and meaningful recognition.
• Effectively manage the employee lifecycle processes (recruitment, onboarding, probation, absence reviews, regular one-to-one meetings, performance reviews, etc). Work closely with the HR Business Partner to ensure effective, consistent, timely completion of these processes to support wellbeing and staff growth.

Project Management Office Ownership

• Own the project delivery framework and ensure it is consistently applied (stage gates, RAID, reporting cadence, change control, lessons learned).
• Ensure project plans, risks, dependencies, and resource assignments are well managed and visible to stakeholders.
• Establish/maintain a robust change control model; for larger engagements, chair and own the governance process that assesses overruns and ensures scope changes are matched with appropriate commercials.
• Build a predictable portfolio delivery engine, with strong project discipline, consistent artefacts, accurate status, and early escalation.

Technical Delivery Leadership

• Meet commercial and client satisfaction targets by effectively leading the technical delivery organisation (i.e. ensuring solutions are delivered effectively, securely, and to a consistently high standard, with strong quality assurance from design through deployment and transition).
• Ensure technical teams collaborate effectively with Pre-sales, PMs and Project Coordinators, actively breaking down silos and ensuring joined-up planning, dependency management and customer communications.
• Drive standardisation and repeatability through templates, playbooks, reference architectures, and delivery patterns to improve margin and predictability.
• Ensure end-to-end delivery accountability, including robust knowledge transfer into Managed Services and effective Service Desk enablement, as well as the creation and maintenance of all required documentation and knowledge articles.

Customer Leadership & Stakeholder Management

• Act as a senior escalation point and ensure customer outcomes through clear governance, reporting, and expectation management.
• Serve as executive sponsor for key customers, representing DA in senior stakeholder forums and translating business needs into prioritised delivery roadmaps.

Commercial & Operational Performance

• Own end-to-end Professional Services performance, including profitability targets and operational success metrics.
• Establish and maintain reporting that show utilization (forecast vs actual), margin, project profitability, delivery performance, and pipeline coverage.
• Ensure statements of work (SOWs) accurately reflect scope, effort, skill mix, and delivery method; reducing leakage and improve estimating accuracy as services evolve.
• Optimise resourcing across PMO and technical delivery to balance customer demand, staff wellbeing, and financial outcomes.

Pre-sales Support & Service Evolution

• Partner with Sales to validate delivery approaches and ensure commitments are deliverable and scalable.
• Assist the Pre-sales function in creating repeatable solutions and delivery processes (including adoption of automation/AI where appropriate) to accelerate time-to-value.
• Build relationships with key partners/suppliers and help evolve the service catalogue and technical capabilities, facilitating the ability to flex resources to changing demands.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Essential

• Proven senior leadership experience running a Professional Services function within an MSP / IT consultancy environment.
• Demonstrable commercial acumen: estimating, margin management, utilisation control, and delivery governance.
• Excellent stakeholder management and ability to operate credibly with senior customer leaders.
• Strong delivery-method expertise (Prince2 / PMP / Agile hybrid) and ability to embed scalable processes.

Desirable

• A credible understanding of Microsoft cloud ecosystem (M365 / Azure / Modern Workplace), security/compliance considerations, and transition to operations.
• Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NIST or similar) and delivery governance in regulated environments.

Qualification, skills & experience

• Relevant project/programme leadership certifications (e.g., PRINCE2, PMP, MSP, Agile/Scrum)
• Degree-level education or equivalent experience

Leadership Qualities

title: Early Help Key Worker
description:
Job Description

Salary range: Grade 8 (£41,511-£43,449p.a.) plus fantastic benefits

Contract: Permanent

Hours of work: 36 hours per week

Location: Croydon

Job Purpose

This role will provide support for families across the continuum of need. This service aims to assist families in recognising and accessing relevant support networks which will enable them to enjoy and achieve a good standard of family life and wellbeing without the need for input from Children’s Social Care. Working within a supportive management structure, you will be responsible for the delivery of ‘whole family’ assessments and interventions using a ‘Team Around the Family’ framework. Through the use of regular review and management oversight, you will support the progression and achievement of ‘outcomes based’ family plans. Your work will be highly collaborative in nature, relational in approach and heavily influenced by principles of systemic practice.

The service maintains commitment to the delivery of high-quality support through intensive partnership working with families and universal provisions. As a keyworker, you will navigate and broker families’ access to a range of community services including health, education and third sector provisions. Keyworkers work closely alongside locality management, to achieve the delivery of high-quality support for families. You will receive regular case supervision to support and guide the progression of your work with families. In addition, you will benefit from exposure to peer input and influences through your engagement in ‘mixed locality’ reflective discussion groups held on a monthly basis. As a service, we are continually seeking to develop our offer and input to children, young people and their families. We will support you to identify and access opportunities which promote your continuous professional development and enable you to engage with a wide breadth knowledge and learning.

About You

You will be a skilled, experienced and child-focussed practitioner, with a background of relationship-based work with children, young people and their families. You will be a confident practitioner, with broad understanding of child development. You will be able to tailor your knowledge to work with families across a wide age range, including expectant parents, early years, secondary transitions, adolescents and preparation for adulthood. You will be proficient in the undertaking of assessments and able to apply ‘whole family approach’ to the identification and understanding of need. We are looking for individuals who are skilled in the building and sustaining of relationships and able to engage families who may be hesitant or reluctant to work with the service. The work carries aspects of risk management due to the complex and often challenging nature of familial circumstances.

As a key work practitioner you will liaise closely with families, management and wider services to identify potential risks and devise relevant ‘safety plans’ where appropriate to do so. You will carry a mixed caseload of approximately 25 children and manage your work in accordance with Early Help practice standards. Candidates must therefore possess good skills of time management, whilst demonstrating an ability to prioritise the progression of key work tasks. The work itself can be highly rewarding, but also requires a level of responsiveness at times. Applicants with an ability to ‘flex’ and tailor their approach to given scenarios will be welcomed. To be considered for the post, it is essential that you have a proven record of building relationships, responding to crisis and delivering outcomes. It is a pre-requisite that you possess experience in family and/or adolescent work.

Essential Requirements

Experience of undertaking effective decision making that leads to improved outcomes and reduces the risk of safeguarding issues.

Knowledge and understanding of systemic and strengths-based approaches

Extensive knowledge about the wide range of Early Help support available across the continuum of need ranging from universal through to targeted services.

Thorough knowledge and understanding of the research and evidence in relation to child development including issues affecting babies, children and young people’s vulnerability and resilience or sound knowledge in relation to the research.

Knowledge of statutory services and relevant children’s legislation including a high awareness of child protection and safeguarding thresholds, indicators of need and procedures.

title: Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician
description:
Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician

📍 Irvine, Ayrshire (UK Travel Required)

💰 Competitive Salary DOE

🕒 Full-Time | Permanent

About the Opportunity

We are partnering with an innovative Scottish technology business that develops advanced industrial monitoring, condition monitoring and edge-AI solutions for customers across a range of industrial and manufacturing environments.

Combining sensor technology, embedded systems, engineering expertise and data-driven insights, the company is helping organisations better understand the condition, performance and reliability of critical assets through next-generation monitoring technology.

Following continued growth and increasing customer demand, they are seeking a hands-on Condition Monitoring & Installation Technician to support the development, testing, deployment and maintenance of their solutions across the UK.

This is an opportunity to join a growing business at an exciting stage of its journey, where you will have genuine input into product development and play a key role in customer deployments.

The Role

This is a highly varied position combining elements of:

• Industrial instrumentation
• Electrical and mechanical systems
• Sensor installation and commissioning
• Industrial monitoring and machine-health technologies
• Fault finding and diagnostics
• Industrial networking and connectivity
• Product testing and development
• Customer-facing field deployments

Working closely with engineers and product specialists, you will help build, configure, test and deploy monitoring solutions both in-house and at customer sites throughout the UK.

Key Responsibilities

Product Development & Testing

• Build and configure test rigs and demonstration systems
• Assist with prototype development and product improvements
• Assemble electrical and mechanical components
• Prepare equipment for customer deployments
• Support testing, validation and product verification activities

Installation & Commissioning

• Install sensors and monitoring equipment on industrial assets
• Assess machinery and identify suitable locations for monitoring devices and sensors
• Install and configure monitoring hardware and associated equipment
• Commission systems and verify operational performance
• Route, terminate and label cabling to a high standard
• Configure hardware and peripheral devices
• Conduct installation testing and maintain accurate documentation

Fault Finding & Diagnostics

• Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical and connected systems
• Diagnose faults with sensors, communications hardware and field devices
• Investigate connectivity and signal-flow issues
• Support root-cause analysis and corrective actions
• Assist with machine-health assessments through engineering observations and monitoring data

Customer Deployments

• Travel to customer sites across the UK
• Carry out installations and commissioning activities
• Provide technical support during deployments
• Build strong relationships with customers through professional service delivery

Skills & Experience

Essential

• Hands-on experience with machinery, electromechanical equipment, industrial maintenance, installation, instrumentation or a comparable technical environment
• Confidence using hand tools, power tools and basic test equipment safely
• A working understanding of mechanical and electrical systems and how their components interact
• Ability to identify common sensor types and correctly install and connect monitoring devices
• Practical competence in component mounting, basic fitting, sensor wiring, cable routing and tidy, labelled workmanship
• Working knowledge of PCs, basic networking and IT systems
• Understanding of systematic fault diagnosis across physical equipment and connected systems
• Ability to follow drawings, wiring diagrams, equipment manuals and technical instructions
• Clear communication, accurate record keeping and a professional approach to customer interactions
• Sound safety awareness and engineering judgement
• Full UK driving licence
• Ability to commute reliably to the Irvine area and undertake UK-wide travel with occasional overnight stays

Qualifications & Experience Level

Practical or vocational experience is preferred over a degree. An engineering apprenticeship, relevant vocational qualification or equivalent hands-on experience would be suitable.

Around two years of relevant experience is sufficient if you can demonstrate practical engineering ability, sound judgement and a willingness to learn.

Candidates with experience of industrial monitoring technologies, instrumentation, maintenance, automation, sensor installation, commissioning or fault diagnosis will be particularly attractive.

Experience of condition monitoring, predictive maintenance or vibration analysis would be beneficial but is not essential. Training can be provided on the company’s systems and monitoring methodologies.

Industry-recognised certifications such as ISO 18436 Vibration Analysis, or membership of organisations such as BINDT, MIBoC or the Vibration Institute, would be advantageous but are not expected.

Desirable

• Experience of industrial sensors, monitoring equipment or condition-monitoring systems
• Exposure to vibration monitoring, predictive maintenance or reliability programmes
• Awareness of machinery condition assessment and common equipment faults
• Experience working with rotating equipment such as motors, pumps, fans, compressors or gearboxes
• Industrial PCs, data-acquisition systems or edge-computing equipment
• Beckhoff, Siemens, Schneider, Trend or similar automation platforms
• Industrial communications such as Modbus or MQTT
• Basic Linux knowledge or Windows-based industrial system configuration
• Commissioning, customer-site installations or technical demonstrations
• Test-rig maintenance, equipment validation or structured testing activities
• Relevant electrical, machinery-safety or site-working qualifications

You do not need experience of every platform. Full training will be provided on the company’s products and technologies.

What We Are Looking For

The successful candidate will be:

• Hands-on and practical
• Comfortable working independently
• Naturally curious and solutions-focused
• Confident interacting with customers
• Motivated by solving real-world engineering challenges
• Comfortable working around industrial machinery and identifying practical locations for installing monitoring equipment and sensors
• Interested in learning about condition monitoring, reliability engineering and predictive maintenance technologies
• Excited by the opportunity to work within a growing technology business
• Keen to contribute ideas and help improve products and processes

What's on Offer?

• Competitive salary DOE
• Exposure to cutting-edge industrial monitoring, condition-monitoring and AI technologies
• Opportunity to influence product development
• Varied role combining workshop, development and field-based activities
• Significant scope for career development as the business grows
• Collaborative and supportive working environment

Interested?

If you're a hands-on engineer or technician who enjoys solving technical problems, installing technology in real-world environments and seeing the direct impact of your work, we'd love to hear from you.

Whether your background is in instrumentation, industrial maintenance, automation, field service, commissioning or condition monitoring, we encourage you to apply.

• Engagement is measured, acted on, and constantly improved
• Values are not just written they’re lived
• Innovation, inclusion, and giving back are part of the culture

At Eden Futures, we often say we’re a true people’s organisation, and this award shows that we truly live up to it. Our people are the heart of our company. This accreditation reflects how we lead, how we support one another, and how we’ve built a culture where every voice matters.

Our organisation is committed to safe and fair recruitment, safeguarding and protecting those we care for and serve. We are an inclusive employer and make sure all our staff are vetted, selected, trained, and supervised fairly and to a high standard so that they can provide safe, effective, and compassionate care.

At Eden Futures we support vulnerable adults and therefore roles that require contact with our service users are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.

The amendments to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (2013 and 2020) provides that when applying for certain jobs and activities, certain convictions and cautions are considered ‘protected’. This means that they do not need to be disclosed to employers, and if they are disclosed, employers cannot take them into account.

Guidance about whether a conviction or caution should be disclosed can be found on the Ministry of Justice website. It’s a criminal offence for people who are barred from working in regulated activity to apply for roles that require them to work unsupervised with vulnerable adults.

title: Clinical Trials Manager
description:
Job Overview

THIS POST IS FIXED TERM/SECONDMENT FOR 18 MONTHS DUE TO MEET THE NEEDS OF THE SERVICE

IF YOU ARE INTERESTED IN APPLYING FOR THE SECONDMENT POSITION, YOU MUST OBTAIN PERMISSION FROM YOUR CURRENT LINE MANAGER PRIOR TO APPLYING FOR THIS POST.

The Post holder will be responsible for the day to day management and coordination of studies from grant applications to final report on behalf of Chief Investigators within BCUHB. The post holder will be required to manage one or more studies and will ensure the studies complete on time, to target and within budget. The trial manager is responsible for all quality control / assurance processes relating to the study and trial management and will play a pivotal role in ensuring the studies are conducted to the highest ethical, scientific and regulatory standards.

Main duties of the job

The Post holder will lead the execution and coordination of both small single site and large multi-centre clinical trials from development stage. . They will ensure that the trials are managed in line with the research governance policies, requirements of BCUHB, Sponsors and research funders, within the UK policy framework for health and social care research and General Data Protection Principles (GDPR 2018).

The Clinical Trials Manager will work closely with a multi-disciplinary team including Chief Investigators, Principal Investigators, research delivery staff, data managers, administrators and statisticians at Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board as well as hospital sites across the UK; and all relevant clinical trials units in the UK.

Working for our organisation

If you relish a challenge, have a passion to help others or simply fancy a fresh start, then Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) North Wales, has all the right ingredients. The largest health organisation in Wales, providing a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and elective hospital services for a population of around 700,000, across North Wales . Join our team and get the support you need, in line with our Organisational Values and ‘Proud to Lead’ competence framework.

Enjoy being part of working with engaged leadership at all levels, and be assured we are committed to promoting equality and diversity, and are proud to welcome applicants under the “Disability Confident Employer” scheme.

Please check your email account regularly. Successful applicants will receive all recruitment related correspondence via the email account registered on the application form.

The ability to speak Welsh is desirable for this post; Welsh and/or English speakers are equally welcome to apply.

Applications may be submitted in Welsh. Applications submitted in Welsh will not be treated less favourably than an application submitted in English.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

COMMUNICATION AND RELATIONSHIPS

• Act as a point of contact for all partners, stakeholders and regulators which will be internal and external to BCUHB. E.g. UK Clinical Trials Units, HEIs, Health and Care Research Wales, National Institute for Health Research and BCUHB Research & Development Offices.
• Build relationships with Consultants, Clinical Research Fellows and Research Delivery staff both internally and externally communicating complex issues to ensure the research is conducted in accordance with regulation and legislation.
• Work with research teams and associated service departments, managers and R&D personnel both internally and externally, to find ways of overcoming systematic barriers to the set-up, recruitment and maintenance of a comprehensive study portfolio.

MANAGEMENT

• Support Chief Investigators with the preparation of grant applications and development of protocols and study related materials required to conduct research e.g. Patient Information Sheets, Case Report Forms, Trial Master Site File and Site Files.
• Oversee specific budgets, planning for resource needs to ensure that clinical trials are adequately resourced.
• Develop and write trial specific procedures including development of Standard Operating Procedures relating to the management of the studies. Ensure developing studies meet all requirements with regards to the UK policy framework for health and social care research and the EU Clinical Trials Directive. TRIAL COORDINATION AND DATA MANAGEMENT:
• Co-ordinate and oversee the initiation, day to day running and closure of one or more studies.
• Work closely with clinical study teams to ensure studies are conducted in line with the protocol and all applicable regulatory requirements.
• Contribute to the development of all study documentation, under the guidance of the CI and Trial Management Group.
• Develop and/or review other essential clinical research documents including patient information sheets/letters, informed consent forms as well as regulatory paperwork ensuring compliance with relevant SOPs, legislative requirements and guidelines in accordance to BCUHB Policies and Procedures and Good Clinical Practice .

Person specification

Qualifications

Essential criteria

• MSc in relevant field or equivalent experience and training. .
• Knowledge of the requirements of clinical trials during their life cycle from set up to close out
• . Clinical trials terminology and documentation.
• An understanding of the clinical research approval process in the NHS.
• Knowledge of study design.

Experience

Essential criteria

• Recent experience and knowledge of working in the NHS.
• Significant experience of protocol driven quantitative research in a health related field.
• Experience of managing a research project.
• Previous managerial experience.
• Previous direct clinical trials and/or project management experience.

title: Sales Engineer
description:
Be a part of something bigger...

Our Story

Be a part of something bigger...

Radar Healthcare is dedicated to improving patient safety by bringing together the expertise of healthcare professionals and the power of intuitive software. Our innovative platform has been developed in partnership with industry experts to ensure organisations always meet regulatory standards – making it easier than ever for healthcare providers to deliver top-quality care to their patients.

We’re on a mission to become a world-leading health-tech pioneer, and we know that we can only achieve this with the help of talented individuals like you. If you’re passionate about improving healthcare outcomes and want to work in a team of like-minded individuals, we invite you to join us on our journey.

So if you’re up for an exciting challenge and want to be part of a team that’s making a real impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Our Values

At Radar Healthcare, we are all proud of our values-led, open, supportive and inclusive culture. It's just as important that anyone joining our friendly team share the same values as us, to ensure we're all on the same page from day one, so we're looking for people who feel aligned to the following:

🤝🏽 Customer focused with a partnership approach

📖 Open, honest and transparent

🧠 Innovative

🫶🏼 Ethical, trustworthy and caring

Our People & Culture

At Radar Healthcare, we understand and celebrate the fact that our people are our best assets! We are proud to showcase our diverse and passionate talent that encapsulates our vision, purpose and values in our shared mission of innovation in healthcare. We’re an ambitious but caring team, and so supporting our colleagues and partners is always a top priority. Not to mention, we’re not all work and no play – we love getting together to celebrate our achievements together in various settings, whether it be our winter and summer socials, our people-led full company days, team get togethers or simply just interacting and supporting one another over coffee breaks either remotely or in person at our amazing Leeds office.

"We're also super proud to be Great Place to Work-Certified, based on outstanding feedback directly from our team earlier this year, with 91% of the team agreeing that they "would strongly endorse my company to friends and family as a great place to work" Not to mention Radar Healthcare has been named one of the UK’s Top 100 Companies to Work For 2025, one of the Top 20 Tech Companies to Work For, and has received a Two Star Accreditation from Best Companies, recognising ‘Outstanding’ levels of workplace engagement."" 🫶🏼

The Opportunity

Radar Healthcare's new ⭐Sales Engineer⭐

As we continue to grow across the UK and US markets, we're looking for an experienced Sales Engineer to join our commercial team.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who loves engaging with customers, demonstrating software solutions and translating complex challenges into meaningful outcomes. You'll be the product expert within our Sales team, helping prospective customers understand the value of Radar Healthcare through compelling demonstrations, consultative discussions and expert product guidance.

What you’ll be doing to make a difference:

As our Sales Engineer, you'll work closely with Sales Leads throughout the sales cycle, partnering with prospective customers and showcasing how Radar Healthcare can help solve their challenges.

Sales demonstration and opportunity progression

• Lead engaging, outcome-focused product demonstrations for prospective customers across the UK and US markets.
• Tailor demonstrations to the customer’s priorities, buying criteria, workflows, challenges and desired outcomes.
• Support discovery, qualification, sales meetings, workshops and solution discussions throughout the sales cycle.
• Clearly communicate product value, differentiation, functionality and use cases to technical, clinical, operational and executive audiences.
• Partner with Sales Leads to define the sales objective, demonstration strategy, stakeholder needs, risks and agreed next steps for each opportunity.

Sales engineering and solution expertise

• Develop and maintain expert knowledge of the Radar Healthcare platform, product portfolio, value proposition and key customer use cases.
• Maintain a strong understanding of product functionality, approved roadmap developments, integrations, configuration options and solution dependencies.
• Manage high-quality demonstration environments, sales scenarios and supporting data that reflect priority markets and buyer needs.
• Provide accurate and timely responses to product, technical and solution questions raised during live opportunities.
• Keep up to date with healthcare market developments, competitor positioning and customer expectations, using insight to strengthen sales messaging and differentiation.

Support complex sales opportunities

• Work alongside Sales Leads to understand customer requirements and recommend the most appropriate solution approach.
• Help qualify opportunities and identify requirements, dependencies and potential solution gaps.
• Contribute to proposals, tenders, presentations and customer responses.
• Provide product insight during commercial discussions while ensuring commitments align with current product capability and roadmap plans.
• Work alongside Sales Leads to qualify customer requirements, buying drivers and success criteria, and identify the most relevant solution approach.
• Assess product fit, technical requirements, dependencies, risks and potential solution gaps early in the sales cycle.
• Contribute solution expertise and persuasive, customer-specific content to proposals, tenders, presentations and written responses.
• Support commercial discussions with clear solution input, ensuring proposed commitments remain aligned with current product capability and the approved roadmap.

Buyer and stakeholder engagement

• Build credibility and trusted-adviser relationships with clinical, quality, governance, operational, technical, procurement and executive stakeholders.
• Facilitate consultative conversations that uncover customer challenges, decision criteria, priorities and intended outcomes.
• Adapt sales messaging, discovery and demonstrations to suit UK and US healthcare contexts, stakeholder expectations and stages of the buying journey.
• Represent Radar Healthcare at prospect meetings, webinars, conferences and industry events where sales engineering expertise is required.
• Capture prospect feedback, competitive insight and recurring requirements, sharing them with Sales, Product and relevant internal teams.

Enable internal success

• Support the onboarding and ongoing product, solution and demonstration capability of sales colleagues across the UK and US.
• Create and maintain demo scripts, discovery guides, FAQs, objection-handling content, competitive messaging and other sales enablement resources.

Your journey so far...

• Strong previous experience working in a Sales Engineer, Pre-Sales Consultant or similar role within a comparable sales environment.
• Strong experience delivering software of SaaS product demonstrations to a range of stakeholder audiences.
• Ability to understand customer needs and translate them into relevant solution capabilities and business outcomes.
• Experience supporting complex, multi-stakeholder sales opportunities and working as part of a sales team.
• Strong presentation, facilitation, and written communication skills.
• Ability to work flexibly across UK and US sales activity, including occasional travel and meetings across different time zones.

Even better if you…

• Experience within HealthTech, healthcare software or a SaaS environment.
• Knowledge of NHS, private healthcare, social care or US healthcare markets.
• Clinical background or previous experience working in a clinical healthcare setting.
• Understanding of quality, risk, compliance, patient safety or clinical governance processes.
• Experience contributing to bids, tenders, proposals or formal customer evaluations.

The Bigger Picture

Whilst we value professional experiences and qualifications, we’re committed to maintaining a culture of growth and development here at Radar Healthcare. We take into account each candidates demonstrable skillset, drive and ethos so even if you don’t feel 100% qualified for the role – we welcome you to connect with us. We’d love to hear from passionate candidates from all backgrounds that align themselves with our company values and are excited to make a difference in healthcare!

What we offer in return...

💜 Values-led culture - we’re extremely proud of our culture. Learn more about what makes it special here

🏢 Flexible working – We believe in empowering our team to work in a way that suits them best. Whether you’re an early bird or prefer working from home most of the time, we trust you to get the job done around our core hours. We have a base expectation of 1 day per month in the office but outside of this, although we have a fantastic office in the heart of Leeds (complete with a rooftop bar for the summer months), the choice is yours!

🏝️ 25 days holiday (+ Bank holidays) continually increasing with service, plus the option to buy up to a week to suit whatever exotic adventures or big life events you have planned for the year ahead

🎂 Birthdays off and a surprise through the letterbox - we love to make a song and dance about every year around the sun!

🤝🏽 Charity leave – giving back is important to us, so we empower all our team members to support charity every year on company time

🧠 Mental healthcare - Face to face counselling support, an app, and an Employee Assistance Program and many colleagues trained in mental health first aid

👩🏾‍⚕️ Healthcare - Cover with Medicash, you get money back when you spend on health appointments e.g. physio, dental, optician, prescriptions, private GP + more

💛 Life cover – a pay-out of 3x your salary to support your beneficiaries if the worst happened

🚲Cycle, Tech & Home schemes - Save on home and tech purchases by spreading the cost through interest-free salary deductions, with access to products from leading retailers.

💻 Technology – Rest assured, we'll have a laptop all set up and ready for you on your first day. Additionally, in your first week, we’ll conduct a WFH risk assessment to ensure you have everything you need, including a second screen, keyboard, mouse, and any other goodies!

🐶 Dog friendly office

🎈 Socials – we get together as a full company at least four times per year, plus at least once a quarter in individual teams, too. Not including all the fun activities being planned by our newly formed social committee.

🧩 Discounts on cinema, vouchers, gym memberships, days out and much much more

We’re all different, after all!

title: Social Worker, Safeguarding
description:
Birmingham City Council,

Social Worker - Safeguarding

Permanent

Grade C £36,581- £45,529

Working 36.5 hours per week

Consultation grade - subject to formal evaluation under the Pay Equity Review

Golden Hello payment - £1,000 + £5,000 per annum; see below for further details and conditions.

Make a difference where it matters: protect rights, reduce risk and support adults to achieve the outcomes that matter to them.

Are you a Qualified Social Worker with the curiosity, confidence and professional judgement to work with adults where abuse or neglect is suspected? Are you able to hear the person’s voice, analyse complex information and work with partners to make proportionate, defensible decisions?

We are recruiting Qualified Social Workers to Birmingham Adult Social Care’s specialist Safeguarding Service. This is a focused safeguarding role for practitioners who want to develop expertise in statutory adult safeguarding while keeping Making Safeguarding Personal at the centre of practice.

You will work with adults, carers, advocates, providers and partner agencies to establish what has happened, understand current and future risk, agree the outcomes the adult wants and coordinate an appropriate safeguarding response. The work can be complex and sensitive, requiring sound legal literacy, respectful professional challenge and clear recording of decisions and rationale.

About the role:

As a Qualified Social Worker in the Safeguarding Service, you will manage safeguarding work involving different forms of abuse and neglect, complex family and professional networks, competing views, and uncertainty. You will be expected to work in a strengths-based, trauma-informed and person-centred way while maintaining a clear focus on risk and statutory duties.

You will:

• Receive and assess safeguarding concerns, identifying immediate risks and required actions.
• Undertake and coordinate Section 42 enquiries in line with the Care Act 2014.
• Work directly with adults to understand their wishes and achieve person-centred safeguarding outcomes.
• Consider mental capacity, consent, advocacy and safeguarding risks when planning interventions.
• Develop and review safeguarding plans to reduce risk and promote wellbeing.
• Gather, analyse and evaluate information from multiple agencies to inform decision-making.
• Chair and contribute to multi-agency safeguarding meetings and discussions.
• Build effective partnerships with professionals, using constructive challenge where appropriate.
• Identify and respond to complex risks, including domestic abuse, self-neglect, exploitation and organisational abuse.
• Escalate urgent concerns and unresolved risks through appropriate channels.
• Maintain accurate, analytical records and reports that evidence decision-making and outcomes.
• Contribute to quality assurance, learning and service improvement activities.

About You

You will be a qualified and registered Social Worker who can combine empathy and relationship-based practice with confident risk analysis and clear professional decision-making. Experience of adult safeguarding is desirable, but we also welcome applicants with strong transferable adult social work experience and a clear commitment to developing specialist safeguarding practice.

You will have:

• Social Work England recognised qualification (such as CQSW, DipSW, CSS or equivalent) and current registration number
• Experience working with adults, carers and partner agencies.
• Knowledge of adult social care legislation, including Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005, Human Rights Act 1998
• Ability to assess risk, analyse information and make sound, evidence-based decisions.
• Strong communication skills, including handling sensitive conversations and professional challenge.
• Ability to maintain accurate records and produce clear, analytical reports.
• Understanding of Making Safeguarding Personal and strengths-based practice.
• Ability to manage competing priorities, urgent situations and statutory deadlines.
• Commitment to equality, professional development and reflective practice.

What you'll bring:

Most importantly, you will bring a person-centred and professionally curious approach. You will listen carefully, avoid assumptions, recognise strengths and work alongside adults rather than doing safeguarding to them.

You will be able to hold respectful but difficult conversations, remain focused when situations are uncertain or contested, and understand when risk requires escalation. You will also recognise that effective safeguarding depends on shared ownership across agencies, with clear boundaries, responsibilities and handovers.

Why Birmingham City Council?

This is an opportunity to join a specialist service where your professional judgement can make a direct difference to adults experiencing abuse or neglect. You will work across organisational boundaries, contribute to high-quality statutory practice and help strengthen safeguarding responses across Birmingham’s diverse communities.

If you are looking for a role that combines direct work with adults, complex risk analysis, multi-agency partnership working and continuous learning, we'd love to hear from you.

Onboarding Process: Please note as part of our onboarding process, the successful candidate will be required undergo a series of background checks with Experian Including Experian Right to Work, and Digital ID verification. These are essential pre-employment requirements.

Please upload an up-to-date CV and Supporting Statement via the attachments part of your application. The Supporting Statement should outline how you meet the criteria for the role through your personal qualities, skills and experience and include your motivation for applying to the post. Note the Personal Statement should be no more than 1500 words. Unfortunately, we cannot consider any applications without a CV and Personal Statement attached

Birmingham City Council is an accredited Disability Confident Leader employer, and we are committed to employing, retaining and developing all of our people.

We want to ensure your recruitment journey with us is a positive and equitable one, so please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments, additional support, accessibility needs, or if there is any way in which we can support you through your application.

For any informal enquires please contact: Resourcing@birmingham.gov.uk

A Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check will be undertaken.

Proof of Right to work in the UK will be required for all applicants in accordance with UK Home Office requirements, before any employment offer can be confirmed.
